title: Modelling Maternal-to-Zygotic Transition Dynamics to Identify Common Gene Expression Baselines in Zebrafish Development.
abstract: We propose a semi-mechanistic ODE-based transcription model for zebrafish embryogenesis that captures common baseline expression dynamics by integrating the maternal-to-zygotic transition mechanism. We fitted this model to a time-course RNA-seq dataset of D. rerio spanning early developmental stages until 120 hpf. Using the inferred model parameters, we identified common gene expression pattern using fuzzy c-means clustering and compared these with clusters stemming from a shape-based approach using smooth trajectories. We show that the ODE-parameter-based approach improves to biological interpretability by linking clusters to underlying regulatory mechanism, such as the timing of zygotic genome activation, thereby generating more precise expression clusters. However, the results also revealed technical biases of the time-course data, originating from the poly(A) enrichment step.

title: Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M2 in the anterior cingulate cortex mediates central sensitization after peripheral nerve injury.
abstract: The activation of α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor subunit glutamate A1 (GluA1) in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) has been implicated mechanical sensitization after peripheral nerve injury. Separately, muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (mAChR) activation is known to initiate downstream signaling cascades that regulate glutamate receptor expression, trafficking, and upregulation. To investigate the role of mAChR in the ACC under neuropathic pain conditions, we employed chronic constriction injury (CCI) modeling combined with mechanical allodynia tests, in vitro whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, western blotting, immunofluorescence staining, and RNA interference techniques in this study. Our results demonstrated that CCI led to increased amplitude and frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents, along with elevated GluA1 protein levels in the ACC. Notably, expression of mAChR M2 in the ACC was not significantly altered following nerve injury. However, conditional knockdown of mAChR M2 in ACC excitatory neurons significantly reduced GluA1 expression and attenuated neuropathic pain development in mice. These results indicate that the activity of mAChRs M2 in ACC pyramidal neurons is necessary for GluA1-dependent synaptic strengthening and pain sensitization. Thus, targeting this receptor may represent a viable strategy for alleviating ACC-mediated chronic pain.

title: Phosphorylated SCD functions as a nuclear chaperone to inhibit MTA2 activity and promote tumor malignancy.
abstract: Phosphorylation dysregulation is a marker of cancer serving as a key mechanism for tumor malignant progression. However, the mechanism by which the phosphorylation of metabolic enzymes drives metastasis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. Here, we identify phosphorylation of stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD) at serine 198 (pSCD) as a key driver of metastasis in ESCC. Analysis of clinical phosphoproteomic datasets revealed elevated pSCD levels correlating with ESCC metastasis. Functional assays demonstrated that pSCD promotes ESCC metastasis independently of SCD's desaturase activity. pSCD translocates into the nucleus, where it directly binds to the scaffold protein MTA2 within the NuRD complex, suppressing deacetylase activity and reprogramming transcription toward pro-metastatic programs. Integrative ATAC-seq and RNA-seq analyses identified increased accessibility and expression of metastasis-related genes, including MET, KDR, PGF, FGF5, FGF18, and IGF1R. Mechanistically, p110α mediates the phosphorylation of SCD S198, enhancing KPNA2-dependent nuclear import by exposing the nuclear localization signal of SCD through conformational changes. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized PI3K-pSCD-MTA2/NuRD signaling axis that links the phosphorylation of metabolic enzymes to chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation, thereby driving ESCC metastasis.

title: A hybrid mixture approach for clustering and characterizing biomedical data.
abstract: Model-based clustering (MBC) is widely used for identifying latent groups and characterizing heterogeneous structures in biomedical data. However, modern biomedical studies often generate datasets with large sample sizes and many variables, for which standard MBC approaches can be difficult to fit reliably and efficiently. Mixture of factor analyzers (MFA) addresses part of this challenge by representing high-dimensional covariance structures through a few underlying factors, thereby reducing the covariance dimensionality. However, current estimation methods for MFA are often computationally impractical for massive data due to the slow convergence of nested EM-type algorithms. Moreover, many existing implementations require a common number of latent factors across clusters, limiting their ability to capture group-specific structures. We propose a hybrid matrix-free computational scheme for accurate and efficient estimation of Gaussian mixture of factor analyzers, which avoids explicit construction or storage of large covariance matrices. We further develop a generalized version that allows different clusters to have varying numbers of factors, providing additional flexibility for group-specific characterization. Simulation studies show that the proposed approach achieves substantially faster convergence than the existing method, especially in high-dimensional settings, while preserving high clustering and estimation accuracy. Applications to the Wisconsin breast cancer dataset, a lymphoma gene-expression dataset, and a human brain single-cell RNA sequencing dataset demonstrate accurate identification of benign/malignant breast tumors, lymphoma subtypes, and neuronal and astrocytic cell populations. The fitted factor-loading structures reveal biologically meaningful differences in nuclear morphology for breast tumors, with malignant samples showing stronger irregularity-related variation, group-specific gene-expression heterogeneity among the three lymphoma subtypes, and distinct patterns of transcriptional variation between neurons and astrocytes, with neuronal variation reflecting a broader set of coordinated transcriptional directions and astrocytic variation concentrated in a more compact latent structure.

title: MIR99AHG suppresses lung cancer progression by restricting SCD1-dependent lipid biogenesis.
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are important regulators of tumor progression, but their roles in lipid metabolic reprogramming remain incompletely defined. Here, we identified MIR99AHG as a downregulated lncRNA in lung cancer. Functional assays showed that MIR99AHG knockdown promoted, whereas MIR99AHG overexpression inhibited, cell proliferation, colony formation, migration and invasion. Mechanistically, RNA pulldown followed by mass spectrometry identified SCD1 as a MIR99AHG-associated protein. MIR99AHG depletion did not markedly alter SCD1 mRNA levels, but increased SCD1 protein fluorescence intensity, suggesting post-transcriptional regulation. Functionally, SCD1 knockdown reversed MIR99AHG depletion-induced lipid accumulation, triglyceride production, cell growth, migration and invasion. Together, these findings reveal a MIR99AHG-SCD1 regulatory axis that suppresses lipid biogenesis and malignant progression in lung cancer.

title: Single-cell multi-omics identify OTP and NOVA1 as regulators of leptin action in hypothalamic feeding circuits.
abstract: Leptin acts directly and indirectly on multiple neuronal populations to regulate feeding and numerous other physiologic functions. However, our understanding of how a single circulating signal coordinates diverse neuronal populations across multiple circuits is limited. To further elucidate how leptin reshapes molecular states in its direct and indirect neural targets, we combined time-resolved single-nucleus transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility profiling to map leptin-induced transcriptional and chromatin state changes across individual neurons in two key hypothalamic nuclei: the arcuate nucleus (ARC), which contains the majority of leptin receptor (LepR) neurons, and the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVH), an established downstream target of ARC LepR neurons. We found that leptin treatment of leptin-deficient ob/ob mice does not alter neuronal identity, but instead induces coordinated, cell-type-specific transcriptional and regulatory state changes that propagate hierarchically from the ARC to downstream PVH neurons. Integrating RNA velocity, cis-regulatory analysis, and cell-cell communication inference revealed that leptin modulates hypothalamic circuit architecture by selectively strengthening specific interactions while pruning broadly distributed, low-specificity signaling. Although leptin broadly activated STAT3 signaling across LepR neuronal subtypes, integrated multi-omic analyses revealed that activation of STAT3 engages distinct downstream regulatory programs in different neuronal populations, often with opposing physiological functions. Functional analyses identified the homeobox transcription factor OTP, a leptin-responsive regulator selectively induced in AGRP neurons, as a critical mediator of leptin-mediated inhibition of hunger-promoting AGRP neuronal activity and feeding. In parallel, unbiased analysis of PVH neuronal state transitions shows that NOVA1, an RNA-binding protein primarily expressed in inhibitory neurons, is regulated by leptin and alterations of NOVA1 expression bidirectionally control food intake and body weight. Together, these findings define a multi-layered regulatory framework through which leptin regulates hypothalamic feeding circuits to control energy balance.

title: Maternal E-Cigarette Exposure Exacerbates Neonatal Ischemic Brain Injury Through the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 Axis.
abstract: Neonatal ischemic stroke is an important cause of mortality and long-term neurological morbidity in infants. Maternal smoking and e-cigarette exposure are recognized risk factors for adverse neonatal outcomes, but the mechanisms underlying increased susceptibility to ischemic brain injury remain unclear. This study investigated whether dysregulation of the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 axis contributes to this susceptibility. Pregnant rats were exposed to e-cigarette aerosols from embryonic day 4 to 20. Studies were conducted in male offspring on postnatal day 10. Baseline molecular changes were assessed using microRNA sequencing, quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, Western blotting, RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) and luciferase reporter assays. Ischemic injury was evaluated following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). Flow cytometry and molecular analyses were performed to characterize associated cellular changes. The effects of in vivo miR-30c-5p mimic administration, Neurod1 knockdown, and miR-30c-5p inhibition were also investigated. Maternal e-cigarette exposure increased tMCAO-induced infarct size and was associated with increased apoptosis and senescence-associated changes, together with reduced expression of markers of neurogenesis and synaptic development. Under baseline conditions, microRNA profiling and molecular analyses revealed increased miR-30c-5p expression and decreased Neurod1 mRNA and protein levels in the neonatal brain. RISC and luciferase reporter assays supported an interaction between miR-30c-5p and Neurod1 mRNA. In vivo administration of a miR-30c-5p mimic reduced Neurod1 expression and increased infarct size, whereas Neurod1 knockdown independently exacerbated ischemic injury and associated cellular changes. Conversely, inhibition of miR-30c-5p restored Neurod1 expression, reduced infarct size, and ameliorated associated pathological changes. Maternal e-cigarette exposure is associated with baseline dysregulation of the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 axis and increased susceptibility to neonatal ischemic brain injury in male rats. These findings suggest that this regulatory axis may contribute to the effects of prenatal e-cigarette exposure on the developing brain and may increase susceptibility to neonatal ischemic stroke.

title: Scalable Multi-omics Diagonal Integration from Self-Mapping.
abstract: Diagonal integration seeks to align single-cell multi-omics datasets in which distinct modalities, such as RNA and protein, are measured in different cells. Unlike horizontal integration, these datasets lack direct cell-cell correspondences and complete feature mappings across modalities. Leading methods for weak-linkage integration often infer anchor cells between modalities by searching for cross-modal similarities through predefined feature links, then use these anchors to guide alignment. Their required matching or anchor refinement can become computationally burdensome at atlas scale. Here, we introduce a novel self-mapping technique, a mechanism that aligns modalities by mapping each computationally decoded cross-modality omics profile prediction to its own observed inputs. We implement this strategy in SCALEMAP, a scalable, modality-agnostic method for diagonal integration. Across transcriptomic, epigenomic and proteomic benchmarks, SCALEMAP matches or outperforms leading alternatives while requiring substantially less runtime and memory. In large-scale experiments, SCALEMAP integrates more than 1.5 million multi-omic profiles in less than 5 minutes with under 20 GB peak memory, which enables rapid synthesis of massive single-cell multi-omics resources into unified biological representations.

title: Epigenetic Mechanisms Inhibit Smad7 and Contribute to Fibrosis in Crohn's Disease.
abstract: TGF-β1 is a central regulator of profibrotic gene expression, extracellular matrix deposition, and the development of intestinal fibrosis in patients with fibrostenotic Crohn's disease (CD). Unlike the increased expression of Smad7 in mucosal and lamina propria monocytes, where it impairs Treg function, mesenchymal cells from patients with fibrostenotic CD do not exhibit elevated Smad7 expression and instead display sustained TGF-β1 signaling. We therefore sought to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the unexpected silencing of Smad7 in fibrostenotic CD. Subepithelial myofibroblasts (SEMFs) and muscularis smooth muscle cells were isolated from paired normal and affected ileal tissues obtained from the same patients with each Montreal phenotype of CD, as well as from non-CD controls. Gene expression, RNA-binding affinity, transcriptional activity, promoter methylation, protein levels, and the mechanisms that regulate Smad7 expression were evaluated in ex vivo tissues and primary cultured cells. MicroRNA-21 (miR-21) localization was assessed by RNAscope. miR-21-mediated suppression of Smad7 was investigated using antagomiR-21. Smad7 silencing through promoter hypermethylation was confirmed using 5-Azacytidine treatment and DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1) knockdown. Smad7 lysine acetylation and Smurf1/2-mediated ubiquitination were examined using selective inhibitors and proximity ligation assays. In SEMFs from patients with fibrostenotic CD, aberrant silencing of Smad7 resulted from DNMT1-dependent promoter hypermethylation and pSmad3-driven, miR-21-mediated degradation of Smad7 mRNA. In addition, Smurf1/2 promoted ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of acetylated Smad7 protein. Inhibition of miR-21 with antagomiR-21 restored Smad7 expression and reduced TGF-β1-dependent profibrotic gene expression. Likewise, demethylation with 5-Azacytidine or knockdown of DNMT1 induced Smad7 promoter hypomethylation and restored Smad7 expression. Furthermore, modulation of the balance between p300 acetyltransferase and histone deacetylase 1 (HDAC1) stabilized Smad7 protein by protecting it from degradation. A distinctive pattern of epigenetic silencing and post-translational regulation of Smad7 was identified in patients with fibrostenotic CD. These mechanisms collectively promote unrestrained TGF-β1 signaling by suppressing Smad7 expression and stability in SEMFs, thereby contributing to the development of intestinal fibrosis.

title: hsa_circ_0007766 regulates tumorigenesis and metastasis of breast cancer via miR‑1301‑3p/DNMT3B feedback loop.
abstract: The development and progression of breast cancer (BC) are intricately linked to the dysregulation of non‑coding RNA expression and aberrant methylation patterns. In the present study, the functional mechanism of hsa‑circ‑0007766 was uncovered, identifying it as an oncogenic circular RNA (circRNA) in BC. Reverse transcription‑quantitative polymerase chain reaction was employed to assess the expression levels of hsa‑circ‑0007766, miR‑1301‑3p and DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) 3B in BC cell lines. Additionally, MTT, wound healing and Transwell assays were utilized to explore the roles of hsa‑circ‑0007766 and miR‑1301‑3p in cellular proliferation, migration and invasion. Protein expression was quantified using western blot analysis, while dual‑luciferase reporter assays were conducted to confirm the interaction between hsa‑circ‑0007766 and miR‑1301‑3p or DNMT3B. The present findings revealed that hsa‑circ‑0007766 and DNMT3B are upregulated, while miR‑1301‑3p is downregulated in BC cell lines. Functionally, the knockdown of hsa‑circ‑0007766 significantly inhibited cell proliferation, migration and invasion. hsa‑circ‑0007766 was identified as a sponge of miR‑1301‑3p, and the inhibition of miR‑1301‑3p reversed the suppressive effects of hsa‑circ‑0007766 knockdown on BC progression. Moreover, DNMT3B, which is upregulated in BC, was found to be a downstream target gene of miR‑1301‑3p, regulating cell proliferation, migration and invasion. Notably, a positive feedback loop between miR‑1301‑3p and DNMT3B was observed. In conclusion, the present study demonstrated that hsa‑circ‑0007766 regulates cell proliferation, migration and invasion in BC cells through a miR‑1301‑3p/DNMT3B feedback loop. These findings offer novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying BC and may pave the way for the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Osmotic stress-induced phase separation drives OsbZIP13 condensates to reprogram transcription from growth to stress adaptation.
abstract: Osmotic stress forces plants to balance photosynthesis and abscisic acid (ABA) accumulation, but the molecular mechanisms coordinating these opposing responses remain unclear. We investigated the role of the rice (Oryza sativa) transcription factor OsbZIP13 in this trade-off. To get insights into the mechanisms, we combined RNA-seq, ChIP-seq and live-cell imaging to dissect rice transcription factor OsbZIP13 as an osmotic sensor functional switch from photosynthetic growth to osmotic stress adaptation. We show that OsbZIP13 transcription is repressed by osmotic stress, while its protein is stabilized and undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) to form nuclear condensates. These condensates switch OsbZIP13 binding from photosynthetic gene promoters to the OsNCED3 promoter, activating ABA biosynthesis and repressing photosynthesis. OsbZIP13 overexpression (OsbZIP13-ox) enhances drought and osmotic tolerance, higher photosynthetic rates and improved yield with delayed heading, whereas knockout mutants are hypersensitive. Our findings reveal that osmotic stress-induced condensation of OsbZIP13 acts as a molecular switch to balance photosynthesis and osmotic stress adaptation, offering a promising target for breeding climate-resilient rice.

title: Biomimetic-Inspired Limited Basement Membrane Proteolysis Modulates Mesenchymal Stem Cell Transmigration while Preserving Endothelial Quiescence on Xenogeneic Extracellular Matrix Scaffolds.
abstract: The success of tissue-derived acellular extracellular matrix (ECM) scaffolds for blood contacting applications depends on preserving basement membrane (BM) integrity to promote quiescent reendothelialization, while simultaneously facilitating progenitor cell infiltration to repopulate underlying stromal compartments. However, achieving this balance remains a central challenge in vascular tissue engineering. This study aimed to determine whether biomimetic-inspired limited proteolysis using proteinase K (PK) can modulate BM structure to enhance mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) transmigration (i.e., stromal repopulation), while maintaining scaffold integrity and BM-mediated endothelial cell (EC) quiescence. Antigen-removed bovine pericardium (AR-BP) ECM scaffolds were treated with increasing PK concentrations (0-20 µg/mL) and characterized using histology, immunofluorescence for bovine BM components (i.e., laminin and collagen IV (Col IV)), and biomechanical testing. Human MSC transmigration was assessed through DAPI staining, quantitative migration analysis, and migratory mechanism probed using RNA sequencing. Human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) were seeded to evaluate EC polarization, adherens junction organization, new BM synthesis (i.e., human laminin and Col IV), nitric oxide production, and inflammatory response. PK treatment (2-5 µg/mL) preserved BM components and mechanical properties, while significantly enhancing MSC migration compared to untreated scaffolds. Excessive proteolysis (20 µg/mL) disrupted BM structure and compromised mechanical stability. Transcriptomic analysis identified 114 upregulated genes in PK-treated scaffolds, predominantly associated with cell migration, proliferation, and cytoskeletal remodeling. Immunofluorescence staining demonstrated that HAECs formed a quiescent, polarized monolayer with organized adherens junction proteins, preventing platelet activation and preserving nitric oxide production on PK 0-2 µg/mL scaffolds, whereas higher PK levels impaired endothelial function, increased new BM production, platelet activation and inflammatory signaling. These findings demonstrate that biomimetic-inspired limited BM proteolysis defines a functional threshold that optimizes scaffold bioactivity. Fine-tuning proteolytic processing enables a balance between structural preservation and cellular permissiveness, providing a potential strategy to promote functional human cellular repopulation, integration and remodeling in future cardiovascular applications. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: A key challenge in vascular tissue engineering is balancing reendothelialization with stromal recellularization. The basement membrane, while essential for maintaining healthy endothelial function, acts as a barrier to stromal cell migration. Here, we demonstrate that controlled enzymatic modulation can selectively "permeabilize" the basement membrane, enabling stem cell transmigration and stromal repopulation, while preserving mechanical integrity and supporting endothelial health. Importantly, we identify a functional threshold that governs this balance, beyond which structural and functional compromise occurs. These findings provide a simple and translatable strategy for improving vascular graft design, with significant implications for enhancing integration and long-term clinical performance.

title: Targeting METTL3 protects against acetaminophen-induced liver injury through HAPTOGLOBIN/CD163 macrophage axis.
abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is the most common cause of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), with limited treatment options. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is the most abundant internal epitranscriptomic modification in eukaryotic RNAs and is involved in various physiological and pathological processes, serving as a potential therapeutic target for many diseases. However, little is known about the role of m6A in DILI. Here, we found that intrahepatic expression of Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the core catalytic subunit of RNA m6A methyltransferase complex, was elevated in patients with DILI and mouse DILI models. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of METTL3, achieved via either Alb-CreERT2-driven recombination or adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated delivery of Cre, significantly protected from APAP-induced hepatotoxicity in both male and female mice. Mechanistically, hepatic METTL3 deficiency reduced m6A deposition on acute-phase protein haptoglobin (Hp) transcripts and promoted Hp transcription and translation in hepatocytes. Increased HP secreted by hepatocytes bound to its receptor CD163, expressed explicitly on macrophages, and induced highly phagocytic and anti-inflammatory polarization of macrophages, finally reducing APAP-induced hepatic injury. Moreover, two different METTL3 inhibitors, JNJ64619178 and STM2457, effectively alleviated APAP-induced liver injury. Our study thus demonstrated that hepatic inhibition of METTL3 protected against APAP-induced liver injury by promoting the cross-talk between hepatocytes and macrophages through HP/CD163, underscoring the potential of targeting METTL3 as a promising therapy for APAP overdose.

title: Advanced Medical Therapeutic Approaches to Treat Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCSs) encompass obstructive and non-obstructive coronary artery disease, including epicardial atherosclerosis, coronary microvascular dysfunction, and coronary vasospasm, which may lead to angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, heart attack, and sudden death. Understanding the pathophysiology of CCS has led to targeted therapeutic approaches aimed at managing dyslipidemia, inflammation, and thrombus formation to reduce cardiovascular burden and mortality risk. This review aimed to explore advanced and emerging therapeutic strategies for the treatment of CCS, including advanced lipid-lowering therapies, Lp(a)-lowering RNA agents, novel anti-inflammatory agents, including interleukin-6 (IL-6)-targeted therapy, Factor XIa-targeted antithrombotic therapy, cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitors (CETP), angiopoietin-like protein 3 (ANGPTL3) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), nanoparticle-based targeted therapies, and microbiome-modifying therapies. This review situates each therapeutic agent within the 2024 ESC and 2023 ACC/AHA chronic coronary syndrome guidelines and, because regulatory approval, guideline recommendations, and cardiovascular outcome evidence are distinct concepts, considers each separately: high-intensity statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, low-dose colchicine, and semaglutide are approved and guideline-recommended for defined populations with outcome-trial support; inclisiran and bempedoic acid are approved and guideline-endorsed as add-on lipid-lowering therapies, although inclisiran's dedicated cardiovascular outcomes trial remains ongoing; and pelacarsen, olpasiran, lepodisiran, zerlasiran, ziltivekimab, and obicetrapib remain investigational, with regulatory approval and guideline recommendations contingent on cardiovascular outcomes trial (CVOT) data. Nanomedicine- and microbiome-based approaches remain preclinical or early-phase and are considered hypothesis-generating. Despite promising advances, long-term safety, optimal patient selection, and cardiovascular outcome benefits remain uncertain. Future research should prioritize outcome-driven trials and personalized therapeutic strategies to address residual cardiovascular risk.

title: Dataset on the design and functional evaluation of INHBE-targeting small interfering RNAs.
abstract: Abdominal obesity is a major risk factor for metabolic disorders. Human genetic and transcriptomic studies have identified the inhibin beta E subunit (INHBE), a liver-enriched gene encoding activin E, as a potential regulator of body fat distribution and metabolic homeostasis. These findings highlight INHBE as a potential therapeutic target for RNA interference (RNAi)-based interventions. This study aimed to design and evaluate INHBE-targeting siRNAs. This was done by first using chemically synthesized siRNAs as a reference, followed by the establishment of an enzymatic in vitro transcription (IVT) workflow for siRNA synthesis and comparison of the gene-silencing efficiency of chemically synthesized and enzymatically synthesized siRNAs in human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cells. Gene-silencing efficiency was assessed by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) to quantify INHBE mRNA expression. Among the eight candidates, siRNA-3 and siRNA-6 produced the strongest inhibitory effects on INHBE knockdown. However, chemically synthesized siRNAs produced more consistent and reproducible knockdown effects, whereas IVT synthesized-siRNAs showed greater variability across experiments. In conclusion, the dataset includes the siRNA target sequences and corresponding INHBE expression data, providing a resource for comparing siRNA candidates and evaluating the effects of target-site selection on INHBE silencing.

title: Mechanism of the lncRNA-FGD5-AS1/miR-383-5p/SOCS3 signaling axis in periodontitis.
abstract: lncRNAs served as crucial regulators in the pathogenesis and advancement of periodontitis. This study aimed to investigate whether lncRNA-FGD5-AS1 affects the proliferation and inflammatory response of LPS-induced HPDLSCs in vitro by regulating the miR-383-5p/SOCS3 axis. To set up an in vitro model of inflammation, HPDLSCs were treated with LPS. Cell proliferation, viability, gene expression (FGD5-AS1, miR-383-5p, and SOCS3), SOCS3 protein expression, and inflammatory cytokine levels were assessed by EdU staining, CCK-8, RT-qPCR, Western blot, and ELISA, respectively. Bioinformatics analysis, dual-luciferase reporter assays, RIP-qPCR, and RNA pull-down assays were further combined to verify the targeting relationships between miR-383-5p and SOCS3, and between FGD5-AS1 and miR-383-5p. Finally, oe-FGD5-AS1 and miR-383-5p mimic cell models were constructed to confirm that FGD5-AS1 regulated LPS-induced inflammatory injury via the miR-383-5p/SOCS3 axis. LPS exhibited a dose-dependent inhibitory effect on both the mRNA and protein levels of SOCS3 in HPDLSCs, and also inhibited cell proliferation. SOCS3 overexpression, in functional rescue experiments, was shown to lower the production of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 and rescue cell proliferation. At the mechanistic level, miR-383-5p directly targeted and downregulated SOCS3. Conversely, FGD5-AS1 served as a ceRNA that upregulated SOCS3 by sponging miR-383-5p. Functional experiments verified that FGD5-AS1 adsorbed miR-383-5p to relieve its inhibitory effect on SOCS3, thereby alleviating the inflammatory response induced by LPS, and exogenous addition of miR-383-5p could reverse this protective effect. By acting as a molecular sponge for miR-383-5p, FGD5-AS1 upregulates SOCS3 expression, thereby suppressing inflammation and enhancing the proliferative capacity of HPDLSCs in an in vitro model of LPS-induced periodontitis. These findings provide a novel theoretical framework for the epigenetic regulation of periodontitis and suggest that this axis may serve as a potential therapeutic target, which warrants further validation in appropriate in vivo models and clinical studies.

title: Gene therapy and RNA-directed medicines in Alzheimer's disease: toward a precision framework for clinical translation.
abstract: Gene transfer and RNA-directed medicines offer distinct approaches to modifying disease-relevant biology in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Existing precision drug-development frameworks require adaptation to account for persistent expression, anatomical distribution, and platform-specific limits on dose adjustment. To propose a modality-specific framework organized around molecular target, biological subgroup, anatomical and cellular delivery, and disease stage, with common requirements for target engagement, clinically meaningful outcomes, and long-term safety. A targeted appraisal of selected clinical, translational, and registry sources was used to develop and illustrate the framework, without a systematic review or quantitative synthesis. The retrieved clinical programs illustrate core domains of the suggested framework: nerve growth factor (NGF) studies showed persistent expression, but postmortem findings in three phase I participants revealed limitations in anatomical delivery; apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε2 gene addition in APOE ε4 homozygotes represents a genotype-directed intervention, whereas brain-derived neurotrophic factor delivery targets vulnerable memory circuits; tau-directed antisense oligonucleotides and RNA-interference approaches targeting tau or amyloid precursor protein expand the range of molecular targets and platforms. The conference-reported phase II CELIA trial findings, consisting of a missed primary dose-response endpoint despite biomarker reductions and exploratory secondary clinical findings, highlight why target engagement and efficacy require separate evaluation. When designing trials in this field, there must be explicitly defined relationships among mechanism, population, exposure, timing, and outcomes before interpreting results. The proposed framework is in its early developmental phase, and its value depends on prospective evaluation, platform-appropriate measures of biological activity, as well as on reassessment of delivery assumptions and therapeutic mechanisms following negative findings.

title: Paneth cell TNF receptor 1 controls zinc deficiency-induced diarrhea.
abstract: Zinc deficiency impairs intestinal homeostasis and alters the gut microbiota composition, ultimately leading to diarrhea. Paneth cells (PCs) are key regulators of intestinal microbial homeostasis by producing antimicrobial peptides, but their role in zinc deficiency-induced diarrhea remains poorly understood. In addition, TNF signaling can regulate PC biology and intestinal barrier function, however, its role during zinc deficiency has not been investigated. This study examined how chronic dietary zinc deficiency affects PCs and the intestinal microbiota, and whether TNF receptor 1 signaling in PCs influences the zinc deficiency-associated intestinal pathology. We established a mouse model based on a zinc-deficient diet (ZDD) and compared it with a standard diet (StD) over 8 weeks. We assessed fecal consistency, PC morphology, the PC transcriptome via bulk RNA sequencing, and ileal microbiome composition via 16S rRNA sequencing. Mice were challenged with peritoneal sepsis or TNF-induced systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS). To study the role of the TNF receptor P55 in PCs, we used mice with a PC-specific P55 deletion (P55PanethKO mice) and wild-type controls (P55PanethWT). Eight weeks of ZDD had mild effects on fecal consistency, PC morphology, and the PC transcriptome. However, 16S sequencing revealed important changes in ileal microbiome composition. These changes made mice significantly more sensitive to challenges that depend on the intestinal bacterial composition, such as peritoneal sepsis and TNF-induced SIRS. P55PanethKO mice on ZDD displayed severe diarrhea. Compared with P55PanethWT controls on ZDD, their PC transcriptome showed a strong STAT/ISRE/IRF signature and a complete absence of the otherwise abundant XBP1s part of the unfolded protein response (UPR). Ileal bacterial isolates were further skewed towards the diarrhea-causing Enterococcus gallinarum. PC-specific P55 is essential for suppressing this STAT/ISRE/IRF response specifically under ZDD conditions. We suggest that in wild-type mammals, the biological activity of TNF on PCs is essential to protect them and to prevent diarrhea. Potential underlying mechanisms are discussed.

title: From Fill to Freeze: Redesigning homeRNA to Enable Robust Sampling and Scalable Downstream Processing Workflows for Remote Blood Transcriptomics.
abstract: In-person research can introduce barriers to participation, including proximity to a study site and scheduling constraints. Our lab developed the homeRNA platform to address these barriers, enabling remote blood collection and RNA stabilization for transcriptomic research. To increase the applicability of homeRNA for large-scale studies, a redesigned version was developed with modifications to 1) improve usability for both participants and downstream processing laboratories, 2) allow for high-throughput manufacturing, and 3) extend the shelf life of the stabilizer tube. In this work, we systematically tested this design against anticipated stresses that can occur throughout a remote study (e.g., high temperature exposure during shipment) to identify and characterize its limitations. We found that the homeRNA device can be prepared and stored at room temperature at least three months in advance of sampling with continued shelf life analysis underway. We also found that the homeRNA platform produces RNA of sufficient quality for downstream transcriptomic analysis under standard shipping durations (i.e., 2 days in transit) and ambient-to-high temperature conditions (i.e., 25-40 °C) and that RNA quality is unaffected by variable blood volumes collected by participants (mean RIN=7.8 in blood volumes 0.25-1 mL). Lastly, we also found that samples can be stored in typical cold storage temperatures and even up to standard room temperature for at least 4 weeks (mean RIN=8.1 after 4 weeks of storage at -80 to 20 °C). This work validates that the new homeRNA platform is robust to many of the expected stresses that samples can experience during remote studies.

title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-discriminative signals. Selected regions are used to generate a gene-by-cell activity matrix. Across 196 paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets, VIGAT outperformed five existing methods in recovering marker-associated accessibility enriched in the corresponding cell populations, demonstrating the utility of VLM-guided visual reasoning for scalable gene activity quantification. VIGAT is implemented as an open-source R package and is freely available at https://github.com/beijie02/VIGAT .

title: Single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of 5xFAD mouse brain maps cell-type-specific transcriptional disruption and preferential rolipram rescue in VIP interneurons.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is characterized by progressive synaptic dysfunction and inhibitory circuit disruption across multiple brain cell types. Rolipram, a selective phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) inhibitor that elevates intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP), activates proteasome, and produces robust procognitive effects in AD mouse models. Still, the cell-type-specific transcriptional mechanisms underlying these effects remain uncharacterized. We profiled 29,664 nuclei from 5xFAD and wild-type (WT) mouse right hemisphere across four conditions: WT Vehicle, WT Rolipram, 5xFAD Vehicle, and 5xFAD Rolipram (0.03 mg/kg/day, 30-day subcutaneous osmotic pump) using the Parse Biosciences Evercode WT v3 combinatorial barcoding platform. Nuclei were clustered into 16 annotated cell type populations using Seurat v5. Disease and rescue effects were quantified as log fold changes (LFCs) across all clusters, with Gene Ontology enrichment assessed using clusterProfiler and transcription factor activity inferred using decoupleR. Disease-associated transcriptional disruption was highly cell-type-specific in its magnitude. Among inhibitory subtypes, VIP/Reln disinhibitory interneurons (n = 149 nuclei) showed the most coherent transcriptional disruption: 289 candidate genes were lower in 5xFAD, with Gene Ontology enrichment concentrated in synapse organization programs, including regulation of synapse structure or activity (padj = 1.5x10^-14, 44 genes), regulation of synapse organization (padj = 1.9x10^-14, 43 genes), and postsynapse organization (padj = 1.1x10^-13, 38 genes). This pathway-level specificity was not reproduced in PVALB or SST interneurons. Astrocytes showed loss of cell-adhesion programs (cell-substrate adhesion padj = 2.4x10^-4, 10 genes). Rolipram rescue was preferential: VIP interneurons yielded 72 true rescue genes and astrocytes yielded 42, with the remaining 14 clusters showing substantially fewer. The cAMP-specific phosphodiesterase Pde7b was disease-context-specifically lower in 5xFAD VIP interneurons (LFC -0.53) and restored by rolipram (LFC +0.54), with WT expression unchanged. decoupleR CREB1 activity inference identified reduced CREB1 activity in 5xFAD VIP interneurons with partial restoration in 5xFAD Rolipram, supporting a stepwise transcriptional cascade in which amyloid pathology reduces cAMP, which suppresses PKA and CREB1 activity. This in turn reduces Pde7b transcription, and rolipram reverses this cascade by blocking cAMP hydrolysis upstream. This single-nucleus atlas provides the first cell-type-resolved characterization of rolipram's transcriptional effects in the 5xFAD brain. VIP disinhibitory interneurons emerge as the most transcriptionally vulnerable inhibitory subtype and the preferential site of rolipram-associated rescue, with the Pde7b/CREB1 signaling axis nominating a tractable, disease-context-specific pharmacological substrate.

title: Accessibility-guided targeting of NRF2-responsive long noncoding RNA NMRAL2P alters a distinct gene expression program and reduces non-small cell lung cancer proliferation.
abstract: Aberrant activation of the antioxidant transcription factor NRF2 promotes non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) survival and therapy resistance, but downstream effectors beyond redox regulation remain incompletely defined. Transcriptome profiling of lung and NSCLC cells identified the pseudogene-derived long noncoding RNA LOC344887/NMRAL2P as consistently associated with NRF2 activity. The NMRAL2P locus produces three predominant, nuclear-localized isoforms whose expression depends on NRF2 across normal lung, lung adenocarcinoma, and lung squamous carcinoma cells. In-cell SHAPE-MaP identified accessible regions within NMRAL2P transcripts, guiding antisense gapmer design. NMRAL2P depletion inhibited NSCLC cell proliferation and increased sensitivity to cisplatin. Transcriptome analysis revealed that NMRAL2P depletion altered a restricted gene expression program involving cell adhesion and MAPK signaling, with responses distinct from those observed following NRF2 depletion. Core NRF2 antioxidant target genes were largely unaffected by NMRAL2P depletion. These findings support a model in which NRF2 induces NMRAL2P to sustain a distinct gene expression program that contributes to NSCLC proliferation and survival. NMRAL2P represents an RNA effector downstream of NRF2 that links oncogenic NRF2 activity to cellular functions beyond canonical antioxidant responses, providing a potential point of intervention in NRF2-active lung cancers and motivating further investigation of the mechanisms connecting this nuclear RNA to signaling pathways.

title: Aging drives senescence in visceral adipose to a greater extent than obesity, instigating multicellular common signaling patterns that impair organ function and drive inflammation.
abstract: Obesity accelerates key hallmarks of biological aging in visceral adipose tissue (VAT), yet age-associated changes in cellular senescence against a background of sustained elevated adiposity remain poorly understood. To investigate these changes, we examined human omental VAT from younger (18-35 years), middle-aged (36-51 years), and older adults (52-75 years) with comparable BMI (40 ± 5 kg/m²) using a cross-sectional design. We integrated bulk and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), Visium HD spatial transcriptomics, and three complementary computational approaches for senescent cell (SnC) identification. VAT from older adults exhibited increased expression of senescence-associated markers, including CDKN2A (p16 INK4a ) and CDKN1A (p21 CIP1 ), as well as enhanced fibro-inflammatory and tissue-remodeling programs. snRNA-seq revealed a non-linear age-associated pattern, with relatively modest differences between younger and middle-aged adults and more pronounced senescence-associated changes in older adults. SnCs were increased primarily in adipose stem/progenitor cells and mesothelium, which also emerged as major intercellular communication hubs. CellChat analyses identified SnCs of multiple lineages converging on shared outgoing signaling programs, implicating inflammatory, extracellular matrix-remodeling, and adipogenic regulatory pathways, including IL-1, IL-6, TGF-β, and WNT signaling. These predicted interactions were accompanied by transcriptional programs involving HIF1A, NF-κB, SMADs, PRRX1, and TP53 in SnCs, as well as consistent upregulation of KDM6B a histone demethylase activating gene expression. Collectively, our findings suggest that aging drives the senescence program to a greater extent than obesity, potentiating tissue dysfunction through coordinated intercellular signaling mechanisms.

title: PCB-Exposed Gut Microbiota Recapitulate Neurobehavioral Deficits and Reprogram Hippocampal Transcriptomic Signatures.
abstract: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are persistent environmental pollutants associated with developmental neurotoxicity and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, whether PCB-induced alterations in gut microbiota contribute to neurodevelopmental toxicity independently of direct chemical exposure remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether transplantation of PCB-associated gut microbiota produces early neurobehavioral alterations and disrupts brain molecular pathways in offspring. Gut microbiota from conventional dams exposed to the Fox River PCB mixture (FRM; 6.0 mg/kg/day) or vehicle were transplanted into germ-free recipient females without direct PCB administration. At postnatal day 7 (P7), offspring underwent ultrasonic vocalization (USV) testing, whole-brain RNA sequencing (n = 4/sex/group), and untargeted serum metabolomics. Untargeted serum metabolomics were also performed in donor dams. PCB-associated fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) significantly reduced offspring USVs, reproducing effects observed following direct maternal PCB exposure. Brain transcriptomics in offspring identified substantially more differentially expressed genes in males (9,339) than females (1,082), including 512 shared genes. Concordantly regulated genes revealed downregulation of neurotransmitter signaling and ion channel pathways alongside upregulation of RNA processing pathways. Male-associated responses involved altered protein synthesis and neuronal signaling, whereas female-associated responses involved DNA repair and extracellular matrix remodeling. Despite these molecular differences, behavioral responses showed no significant sex-dependent effect. Maternal metabolomics revealed increased bile acids and decreased indole-3-propionic acid, highlighting potential AhR-NFκB and bile acid-associated signaling mechanisms. Offspring metabolomics further identified alterations in lipid-associated metabolites and metabolic profiles. Collectively, these findings show that transferring PCB-exposed microbiota reproduces early neurobehavioral alterations and induces shared and sex-biased molecular responses, identifying the maternal gut microbiome as a candidate mediator linking PCB exposure to developmental neurotoxicity.

title: EPB41L4A‑AS1 promotes endothelial dysfunction in preeclampsia through the miR‑26a‑2‑3p/15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK axis.
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy characterized by systemic endothelial dysfunction. Long non‑coding RNA EPB41L4A‑AS1 has been implicated in pregnancy‑related disorders, but its role in PE remains unclear. Our previous work demonstrated that downregulation of miR‑26a‑2‑3p promotes endothelial injury via activation of the 15‑lipoxygenase‑1 (15‑LOX‑1)/p38 mitogen‑activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK) pathway. In the present study, whether EPB41L4A‑AS1 contributes to PE pathogenesis by regulating this axis was investigated. EPB41L4A‑AS1 expression was significantly upregulated in placental tissues from patients with PE and negatively correlated with miR‑26a‑2‑3p levels. Functional experiments revealed that EPB41L4A‑AS1 overexpression suppressed miR‑26a‑2‑3p, activated the 15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK pathway and promoted endothelial dysfunction, effects that were partially reversed by miR‑26a‑2‑3p mimics. In an L‑NAME‑induced PE mouse model, EPB41L4A‑AS1 overexpression exacerbated hypertension, proteinuria, placental apoptosis and oxidative stress, whereas miR‑26a‑2‑3p agomir administration attenuated these effects. Mechanistically, luciferase reporter assays revealed no direct binding between EPB41L4A‑AS1 and miR‑26a‑2‑3p, suggesting an indirect regulatory mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify EPB41L4A‑AS1 as a critical upstream regulator of the miR‑26a‑2‑3p/15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK axis in PE and suggest that targeting this pathway may represent a potential therapeutic strategy.

title: [Mechanistic Study on IL-4 Regulation of Macrophage Polarization via the JAK1-STAT6 Signaling Pathway in Immune Thrombocytopenia].
abstract: To investigate the mechanism by which interleukin-4 (IL-4) regulates macrophage polariza-tion through the JAK1-STAT6 signaling pathway in immune thrombocytopenia (ITP). Sixty female BALB/c mice (8-10 weeks old) were randomized into six groups: control group, ITP group, IL-4c group, IL-4c+ITP group, and inhibitor groups (IL-4c+Jak1i+ITP group, IL-4c+Stat6i+ITP group), with 10 mice in each group. Platelet counts and spleen indices were measured. Flow cytometry was used to analyze M1/M2 macrophage ratio in splenic tissues. RT-qPCR quantified RNA levels of Il4, Il6, Il10, and Jak1. Western blot and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were used to detect protein expression of iNOS, Arg1, Jak1, p-Jak1, Stat6, and p-Stat6. Serum IL-6, IL-10, Jak1 and Stat6 levels were determined by ELISA. The IL-4c group and IL-4c+ITP group showed higher platelet counts than the ITP group and inhibitor groups (all P<0.01). The spleen index in the control group was markedly lower than that in all other groups (all P<0.001). Serum Stat6 cytokine levels were significantly elevated in the IL-4c group compared with those in the ITP group and the IL-4c+Stat6i+ITP group (both P<0.01). Furthermore, serum Stat6 levels in the IL-4c+ITP group were significantly higher than those in the inhibitor groups (both P<0.05). Additionally, IL-10 cytokine expression was significantly higher in the IL-4c group relative to all other experimental groups (all P<0.01). The IL-6 expression level in the IL-4c group was notably reduced compared to the ITP group and inhibitor groups (all P<0.01). Flow cytometry revealed a higher proportion of M1 macrophages in the ITP group compared to control group and IL-4c group (both P<0.05). The IL-4c group demonstrated a higher proportion of M2 macrophages compared to the control group and ITP group (both P<0.01). Western blot and IHC analysis showed that the p-Jak1/Jak1 ratio in the ITP group was significantly lower than that in the IL-4c group and IL-4c+Jak1i+ITP group (both P<0.05). The p-Stat6/Stat6 ratio in the IL-4c group was markedly higher than that in the ITP group, IL-4c+ITP group, and inhibitor groups (all P<0.001). ITP group and inhibitor groups displayed upregulated iNOS protein expression and downregulated Arg1 protein expression compared to the IL-4c group (all P<0.01). Notably, Arg1 protein expression in the IL-4c+ITP group was significantly higher than that in the inhibitor groups (both P<0.05). The RT-qPCR results showed that the expression levels of Il10 RNA in spleen tissues were significantly elevated in both IL-4c group and IL-4c+ITP group compared with the inhibitor groups (all P<0.01). The Il4 RNA expression was significantly higher in the IL-4c group than that in both ITP group and inhibitor groups (both P<0.05). Likewise, the IL-4c+ITP group exhibited significantly higher Il4 RNA expression than that in the inhibitor groups (both P<0.05). Jak1 RNA expression in splenic tissue was significantly elevated in the IL-4c group compared with all other groups except the ITP group (all P<0.05). In contrast, Il6 RNA expression was significantly increased in the ITP group compared with the inhibitor groups (both P<0.05). IL-4c promotes M2 macrophage polarization via the JAK1-STAT6 signaling pathway, thereby ameliorating ITP progression. However, excessive M2 polarization or Jak1-Stat6 inhibition may attenuate therapeutic efficacy.

title: Ehrlichia infection progression drives tissue-independent transcriptional heterogeneity in tick cells.
abstract: Tick-borne diseases pose a significant threat to human and animal health worldwide. In the United States, Ixodes scapularis (I. scapularis) serves as a competent vector for several bacterial pathogens, including Ehrlichia muris eauclairensis (EME). The I. scapularis embryonic cell line ISE6 is widely used to propagate tick-borne pathogens and investigate tick-pathogen interactions and has been characterized as sharing features with neuronal and/or hemocyte-like cells; yet its full cellular complexity and transcriptional identity remain uncharacterized. We hypothesized that EME infection drives time-dependent transcriptional reprogramming in heterogeneous ISE6 cell populations, including changes in synganglion-associated signaling pathways, thereby providing an in vitro system to investigate molecular mechanisms relevant to EME-associated behavioral manipulation in ticks. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified 15 distinct cell clusters within ISE6 cells, revealing substantial transcriptional heterogeneity. Despite this heterogeneity, ISE6 cells lack transcriptional similarity to any known tick tissue, a finding that did not impair their susceptibility to EME infection. EME infection induced time-dependent transcriptional changes: early infection upregulated genes associated with stress adaptation, mitochondrial function, and metabolic pathways, whereas late infection drove broad downregulation of genes involved in cell cycle progression, DNA replication, and cytoskeletal organization. Infection also altered expression of neuropeptide and neuroendocrine signaling components, including pyrokinin-1 receptor, cAMP-dependent protein kinase catalytic subunit 3, and a diuretic hormone receptor, highlighting the potential of ehrlichial infection to disrupt neuronal-like signaling pathways in tick cells. These findings advance our understanding of ehrlichial-vector interactions and support the utility of ISE6 cells as an in vitro platform for studying tick-borne pathogen biology and infection-associated dysregulation of host signaling pathways.

title: Comprehensive analysis of galectin-3 inhibitors GB1107 and pimasertib targeting EMT and cancer stemness pathways to suppress hepatocellular carcinoma progression.
abstract: Galectin-3 (LGALS3), a β-galactoside-binding lectin, plays a pivotal role in regulating physiological and pathological processes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study integrates multi-omics analytics and structure-based drug screening to evaluate Galectin-3 inhibitors for HCC treatment. Transcriptomic data and immunohistochemistry confirmed elevated Galectin-3 expression in HCC tissues, with Kaplan-Meier analysis showing its association with poor survival. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed Galectin-3's role in immune regulation, cancer stemness, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Structure-based screening identified 68 compounds with significant interactions with key Galectin-3 binding sites. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable complex formation between Galectin-3 and inhibitors GB1107 and Pimasertib. In vitro assays demonstrated both compounds significantly inhibited HCC cell viability, colony formation, and migration dose-dependently. GB1107 exhibited stronger cytotoxicity at lower doses, while Pimasertib induced greater apoptosis at higher concentrations. Both compounds effectively downregulated stemness and epithelial-mesenchymal transition markers. These findings suggest Galectin-3 inhibition by GB1107 and Pimasertib disrupts oncogenic pathways, reducing tumor growth and metastatic potential, and offering promising therapeutic strategies for HCC management.

title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations.
abstract: Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

title: Citrullinated antigens induce TLR4-mediated cross-presentation to drive cytotoxic anti-citrullinated antigen CD8⁺ T cell responses in rheumatoid arthritis.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterised by anticitrullinated protein antibodies (ACPAs) and synovial infiltration of activated immune cells. CD8⁺ T cells are increased in ACPA⁺ RA and can recognise major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I-restricted citrullinated autoantigens. We investigated the mechanisms by which citrullinated antigens drive cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cell activation in RA. Single-cell RNA sequencing with paired T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire profiling was performed on T cells from RA blood and synovium. Flow cytometry and immunofluorescence were used to assess oral bacteria-induced neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and citrullinated antigen generation. In vitro coculture assays evaluated cross-presentation of citrullinated antigens by monocyte-derived dendritic cells (MoDCs) and ACPA⁺ B cells. Toll-like receptor (TLR)4 and interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase (IRAK)4 inhibitors were used to assess innate signalling pathways. Single-cell analyses identified clonally expanded cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells shared between RA blood and synovium, with enrichment of activated GZMB⁺IFNG⁺ effector populations in synovial tissue. RA-associated oral bacteria-induced NET formation and peptidyl arginine deiminase-dependent generation of extracellular citrullinated antigens. These antigens were cross-presented by MoDCs and ACPA⁺ B cells through human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I, promoting cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cell activation and clonal expansion. TLR4 signalling enhanced cross-presentation and CD8⁺ T cell responses, whereas IRAK4 inhibition suppressed these effects. Citrullinated antigens also induced interleukin-8 secretion by autoreactive B cells, which can recruit CXCR1/2⁺ cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells. Citrullinated antigens promote TLR4-dependent cross-presentation by MoDCs and ACPA-expressing B cells, leading to HLA class I-dependent activation of CD8⁺ T cells. These findings define a pathogenic pathway that may contribute to synovial inflammation and joint damage in RA.

title: Yishen Zhuangjin Mixture-Containing Serum Modulates Osteogenic and Osteoclastic Differentiation via HMGA1/β-Catenin and CX3CL1/PI3K-AKT In Vitro.
abstract: Yishen Zhuangjin Mixture (YSZJM) is a 13-herb hospital preparation used clinically for disorders associated with bone loss. Its cellular effects and associated signaling responses remain incompletely defined. This study evaluated YSZJM-containing serum (MCS) in mouse MC3T3-E1 osteogenic and RAW264.7 osteoclastic cell models. Cellular metabolic activity and DNA synthesis were assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) assays, respectively. Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) assays were performed to evaluate differentiation. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed with three independent biological replicates per group. Differential-expression and enrichment analyses used the Benjamini-Hochberg correction. High mobility group AT-hook 1 (HMGA1) knockdown and C-X3-C motif chemokine ligand 1 (CX3CL1) overexpression were used to examine the selected signaling axes. Representative EdU images were consistent with greater EdU incorporation in MC3T3-E1 cells and lower EdU incorporation in RAW264.7 cells, and quantitative osteogenic and osteoclastic readouts reflected these changes. At |log2 fold change| ≥ 1 and q < 0.05, RNA-seq identified 1,608 differentially expressed genes in MC3T3-E1 cells and 931 in RAW264.7 cells. Hmga1 was upregulated, whereas Cx3cl1 was downregulated. HMGA1 knockdown attenuated MCS-associated increases in ALP, runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2), and β-catenin. CX3CL1 overexpression attenuated MCS-associated reductions in TRAP and phosphoinositide 3-kinase-protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) activation. MCS therefore modulated osteogenic and osteoclastic phenotypes in association with HMGA1/β-catenin and CX3CL1/PI3K-AKT signaling in these cell-line models. Primary cell, coupled culture, and in vivo validations are required.

title: Learning interpretable compositional features associated with continuous covariates.
abstract: Compositional variation as a function of continuous covariates, such as time, presents challenges for learning interpretable features and accounting for their construction in subsequent inference. Motivated by temporal change in isoform usage in genomics, we introduce IsoVita, a statistical framework integrating covariate-informed balance learning designed for compositional data with complementary tests for abrupt and gradual compositional variation. IsoVita estimates a dominant covariate-dependent direction in the log-ratio coordinates and approximates it as a log ratio of their geometric mean proportions between two learned component groups, linking statistical evidence to explicit component membership. Change point and spline tests evaluate this interpretable feature, while a selection-aware permutation procedure repeats feature construction and testing under each permutation. In transcript-level simulations, IsoVita maintained low empirical false discovery proportions with power to detect differences and change point accuracy improving as temporal signals strengthened. However, the performance depended on trajectory shape and study design. Applications to two human brain bulk RNA-sequencing datasets identified widespread temporal variation in isoform composition while retaining transcript-level interpretability. IsoVita integrates interpretable compositional feature learning with inference along continuous covariates, with potential applications beyond transcriptomics. IsoVita is available as a PyPI package ( https://pypi.org/project/isovita ).

title: Ontology-Based SEA-CDM Integration for Vaccine Clinical Trials: Query, Similarity, and Design Recommendation.
abstract: gov provides valuable information for vaccine research, but fragmented data structures and inconsistent vaccine naming complicate systematic cross-trial analysis. The Study-Experiment-Assay Common Data Model (SEA-CDM) provides a standardized structure for biomedical study data, while biomedical ontologies supply semantic relationships among concepts. We extracted 9,147 vaccine-related study records from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database, mapped their records into SEA-CDM, and linked vaccine products and reported adverse events (AEs) to the Vaccine Ontology (VO) and Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE), respectively. Building on the existing Ontology-based SEA Network (OSEAN), we organized the integrated data into relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph while retaining links to original registrations. We evaluated three applications to assess semantic trial retrieval, context-aware AE ranking and trial similarity, and trial design recommendation. First, VO-based query expansion retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials compared with 16 using exact VO identifier matching. Second, a context-aware AE ranking model incorporating SEA-CDM features and VO-derived vaccine families improved recall@10 from 0.317 to 0.383 over a frequency-based baseline. TransE and CompGCN embeddings achieved Hits@10 of 0.950 and 0.946, respectively, for retrieving trials sharing the same VO identifier within disease-specific candidate sets. Third, an ontology-based clinical trial design recommendation model was developed using several machine learning methods under leave-one-Material-out evaluation across 23 vaccine classes, although performance varied across classes. These findings demonstrate how structural and semantic integration can support multiple clinical trial analyses using vaccine studies as a case study. This framework provides a foundation for extending ontology-supported data integration and analysis to other clinical research domains.

title: Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P.
abstract: Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics data remains an unmet challenge in the post-genomics era, discouraging researchers from pursuing integrative approaches to molecular biology research. Leveraging the power of translation profiling, we present RNA to Translation to Protein (R2T2P), a computational platform integrating genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translation and proteins, including a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. We applied R2T2P to investigate a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), where ectopic expression of the DUX4 retrogene in skeletal muscle triggers significant alterations in transcription and RNA metabolism. We uncovered hundreds of uncharacterized, highly overexpressed RNAs, including antisense and alternative transcripts, and quantified their contribution to translatome and proteome. Re-analysis of expression datasets from patient-derived myotubes and muscle biopsies validated this alternative transcriptome in FSHD patients, adding a reservoir of bona-fide novel molecular actors in a rare disease. Available at https://github.com/nfdata-omics/R2T2P/ , R2T2P is a flexible and powerful workflow in modern integrative biology.

title: Mechanical Tension Promotes Osteogenesis Through CrAT-Mediated Acetylcholine Synthesis in Osteoblasts.
abstract: Rapid maxillary expansion (RME) is a widely used orthodontic approach for correcting maxillary transverse deficiency. Mechanical tension generated during expansion induces bone remodelling and osteogenesis. Our previous studies demonstrated that acetylcholine (ACh) is widely expressed in the maxilla during expansion and may participate in bone remodelling. Carnitine acetyltransferase (CrAT), a key enzyme responsible for non-neuronal ACh synthesis, has been identified in osteoblasts. However, the role of CrAT in regulating ACh synthesis and osteogenic responses under mechanical tension remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of mechanical tension on CrAT expression, ACh synthesis and osteogenic activity in osteoblasts, and to elucidate the regulatory role of CrAT in these processes. CrAT expression in MC3T3-E1 cells was evaluated by immunofluorescence staining. Cyclic tensile strain (12% elongation, 0.1 Hz, half-sine waveform) was applied using a Flexcell FX-5000 Tension System for 0, 1, 4, 8 and 12 h. Extracellular ACh levels, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, and the expression of CrAT and osteogenic markers, including osteopontin (OPN) and osteocalcin (OCN), were assessed using commercial assay kits, quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) and western blotting. CrAT expression was subsequently silenced using small interfering RNA (siRNA), and the effects on ACh production and osteogenic differentiation under static and tensile conditions were evaluated. To determine the working concentration of exogenous ACh, MC3T3-E1 cells were treated with different concentrations of ACh (0-1 mM) for 1, 8 and 24 h, and cell viability was assessed by CCK-8 assay. For the rescue experiment, CrAT-silenced cells were subjected to 8 h of mechanical tension and simultaneously treated with 100 μM exogenous ACh; ALP activity and the mRNA and protein expression of OPN and OCN were then examined. Immunofluorescence staining confirmed that CrAT was predominantly localized in the cytoplasm of MC3T3-E1 cells. Mechanical tension significantly increased extracellular ACh production, ALP activity and the expression of osteogenic markers in a time-dependent manner, with maximal responses observed after 8 h of stimulation. Compared with the control group, CrAT mRNA expression increased by 9.0% and 11.6% after 4 and 8 h of loading, respectively. OPN expression increased by 47.4% and 57.0%, whereas OCN expression increased by 66.5% after 8 h of loading. CrAT knockdown significantly reduced extracellular ACh production, ALP activity and the expression of CrAT, OPN and OCN at both the mRNA and protein levels. Moreover, the osteogenic responses induced by mechanical tension were markedly attenuated following CrAT silencing. In the ACh concentration screening, 0-100 μM ACh had no obvious adverse effects on cell viability, whereas 1 mM ACh significantly decreased viability at 8 and 24 h. Treatment with 100 μM exogenous ACh significantly restored ALP activity and the mRNA and protein expression of OPN and OCN in CrAT-silenced cells under mechanical tension. CrAT is expressed in osteoblasts and participates in the regulation of osteogenic activity. Mechanical tension promotes ACh synthesis and osteogenic differentiation, with maximal effects observed after 8 h of stimulation. Furthermore, CrAT mediates tension-induced osteogenesis, at least partially through regulating non-neuronal ACh synthesis. Importantly, exogenous ACh supplementation rescues the impaired osteogenic response caused by CrAT knockdown under mechanical tension. These findings support the CrAT-ACh axis as a mechanobiological pathway linking mechanical loading to osteogenic responses in osteoblasts.

title: Acetylation-stabilized METTL3 drives anti-PD-1 resistance in lung cancer by promoting CD8+ T cell exhaustion via SPP1 translation.
abstract: Anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (anti-PD-1) therapy is a standard treatment for advanced lung cancer, but its efficacy is often limited by resistance, driven largely by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), a core N6-methyladenosine (m6A) writer, plays a key role in immune regulation and has emerged as a critical modulator of the immunosuppressive tumor niche. Beyond its canonical m6A-catalytic function, METTL3 also exhibits non-catalytic activities and is itself regulated by acetylation. However, its non-catalytic and acetylation-dependent roles in anti-PD-1 resistance remain to be elucidated. METTL3 expression in anti-PD-1-resistant lung cancer cells was assessed by immunohistochemistry and Western blotting. Its in vivo function was evaluated using subcutaneous and orthotopic tumor models under anti-PD-1 treatment. CD8+ T cell exhaustion was examined by single-cell RNA sequencing and flow cytometry. Mechanistic studies included genetic manipulation, polysome profiling, co-immunoprecipitation, and RNA immunoprecipitation. Clinical relevance was validated in human lung cancer samples via immunohistochemistry and multiplex immunofluorescence. Statistical analyses involved unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test, one-way/two-way ANOVA, and Pearson's correlation. METTL3 was upregulated in anti-PD-1-resistant lung cancer cells and it promoted anti-PD-1 resistance in both subcutaneous and orthotopic mouse models. Mechanistically, METTL3 induced CD8+ T cell exhaustion via upregulation of secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1). This occurred independently of its m6A catalytic activity, potentially through direct interaction with eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit H (EIF3H) to facilitate SPP1 translation. Furthermore, METTL3 protein stability was enhanced by lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5)-mediated acetylation, which attenuated ubiquitin-dependent degradation. Finally, critical nodes of the KAT5-METTL3-SPP1 axis were validated in human lung cancer cells, and METTL3 expression positively correlated with KAT5, SPP1, and CD8+ T cell exhaustion markers in clinical samples. We identified a novel KAT5-METTL3-SPP1 axis that drives anti-PD-1 resistance by inducing CD8+ T cell exhaustion. Notably, METTL3 functions through a non-m6A catalytic mechanism involving translation and acetylation. These findings provide new mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance in lung cancer.

title: Using Non-Invasive Human Skin Transcriptome to Discover Chronic Psychological Stress Impact in Chinese Young Adult Females: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Chronic psychological stress (CPS) is associated with impaired skin barrier function and inflammatory skin diseases, but its impacts on healthy young individuals and epidermal molecular changes remain unclear. We aimed to investigate the associations between CPS and facial barrier-related phenotypes in healthy young women and identify associated transcriptomic signatures, with attention to potential age modification. This cross-sectional study enrolled 195 healthy young women in Shanghai, using the Perceived Stress Scale-10 (PSS-10) to classify participants into low (PSS < 10) and high (PSS > 21) stress groups. Facial barrier phenotypes, including trans-epidermal water loss (TEWL), hydration and pH were measured. Tape-stripping samples from the forehead were profiled by RNA-sequencing. Stratified linear regression and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were used to identify candidate pathways and molecules associated with CPS and skin phenotypes. In participants older than 30 years, higher CPS was associated with increased facial TEWL (nominal p < 0.05), suggesting impaired barrier function. WGCNA identified a module (242 genes), which was significantly associated with CPS (nominal p < 0.05) and enriched in 18 immune-related pathways (FDR < 0.05). By integrating pathway scores and gene-phenotype correlations, two pathways (Cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction and Natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity) and eight genes (CCL17, TNFRSF4, CSF2RA, EBI3, CCL22, IL3RA, ITGB2 and IL2RG) were prioritized as candidates showing concordant associations with both CPS and TEWL (FDR < 0.05). Notably, CCL22 showed concordant protein-level changes and increased secretion under combined cortisol and inflammatory cytokine stimulation. These findings suggest age-related effects of CPS on skin barrier phenotypes and provide potential candidate molecular signals for further investigation into stress-related skin phenotypes.

title: A Hierarchical KAN-Augmented Graph Convolutional Model for Inferring Cell-Type-Specific Gene Regulations in Single-Cell Omics.
abstract: Accurate inference of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging due to the complexity of transcription factor (TF)-target interactions and the difficulty in capturing both local and global regulatory dependencies. Here, we present GeneKAN, a novel deep learning framework that integrates multiscale graph convolution with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for robust GRN inference. GeneKAN employs a kernel-based graph convolution module to hierarchically encode gene representations, while KANs model high-order, interpretable TF-target relationships through learnable spline activations. Benchmarking against eleven existing models, and seven scRNA-seq datasets from BEELINE, including diverse cell types, species, and ground-truth networks (ChIP-seq, STRING, LOF/GOF), demonstrates that our proposed GeneKAN achieves state-of-the-art performance in both AUROC and AUPRC. Ablation studies of the proposed model confirm the necessity of each component. Biological validation on human hepatocyte and lung cancer datasets reveals that GeneKAN not only recovers known regulatory interactions with high precision but also identifies functionally relevant hub genes and oncogenic pathways. GeneKAN thus offers a powerful, interpretable, and scalable solution for GRN reconstruction under real-world conditions of data sparsity and noise, with significant potential for advancing systems biology and precision medicine.

title: The synergistic osteogenic effects of FGF1 and BMP2 gene modified bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells in spinal fusion.
abstract: Spinal fusion is essential for treating spinal disorders, but achieving robust bone formation remains challenging. This study evaluated whether FGF1 and BMP2 co-expression in gene-modified BMSCs enhances spinal fusion compared to single-gene approaches. BMSCs were transduced with lentiviruses carrying FGF1, BMP2, or both. Osteogenic differentiation, proliferation, and gene expression were assessed in vitro using staining assays, qPCR, Western blotting, CCK-8, ALP tests, and RNA-seq. In vivo studies in rats evaluated local and systemic protein levels, biosafety, and fusion outcomes via micro-CT, histology, immunohistochemistry, and manual palpation. Dual-modified BMSCs showed significantly higher transgene expression, proliferation, and ALP activity than single-gene or control groups (p < 0.05). RNA-seq revealed upregulated proliferation, angiogenesis, and osteogenic genes, alongside suppressed inflammatory genes, with PI3K-Akt and MAPK pathway enrichment. High local expression occurred without systemic elevation, and no organ abnormalities were observed. Micro-CT and histology demonstrated the most extensive new bone formation in the dual-gene group. Manual palpation confirmed an 80% fusion rate for LV-FGF1-BMP2 versus 20% (LV-BMP2), 0% (LV-FGF1), and 0% (LV-Vector). Dual-gene modification with FGF1 and BMP2 markedly enhances osteogenesis and spinal fusion while maintaining a certain degree of biosafety, representing a promising therapeutic advance over single-gene approaches.

title: Inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell perturbation data by optimizing causal reach of latent mediator dynamics.
abstract: Resolving the causal structure of gene regulatory networks is central to understanding cellular regulation.
