Pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA readouts measure the transcriptional consequences of many interventions in parallel, providing a powerful resource for causal discovery. Combinatorial designs that perturb multiple regulators per cell increase throughput and can reveal responses that single-gene perturbations do not. However, inferring causal gene networks from these experiments remains challenging because gene regulatory interactions are nonlinear, dynamic, and often involve feedback. Thus, attributing the combined effect of several perturbations to individual regulators remains difficult. Additionally, transcriptional regulation is ultimately carried out by proteins, while single-cell perturbation datasets generally measure only RNA levels. Existing methods often simplify regulatory dynamics or rely on assumptions that conflict with gene regulation, such as acyclicity. Moreover, current evaluation practices usually rely on expression prediction error, which is readily computable in real datasets, but does not necessarily reflect graph quality. A complementary metric is needed to assess inferred regulatory connections using observed perturbation responses in real data. To address these challenges, we present CausalODE, a differentiable framework for learning causal graphs from single-cell perturbation data. Our approach incorporates three central insights to improve upon previous methods. First, genes that are differentially expressed when a gene is perturbed should be downstream of the target gene in the regulatory network; we quantify this property with a metric we term causal reach. Second, causal interactions involve transient cellular responses in RNA transcription, splicing, and degradation. Third, gene regulatory interactions are mediated by proteins, whose levels are not directly measured in single-cell RNA-seq experiments. Building on these insights, CausalODE learns a graph that optimizes the causal reach metric, captures transient cellular responses to perturbation, and explicitly models the latent dynamics of protein levels. Together, these components allow nonlinear responses, feedback loops, and time-lagged regulation. Across simulated Perturb-seq datasets with different sparsities and graph structures, CausalODE improves AUPRC and precision among top-ranked edges compared with baselines and competing methods, while achieving competitive AUROC. We introduce a metric to evaluate the causal reach of inferred graphs on real data by measuring how well the graphs explain differentially expressed genes in single-cell perturbation experiments. Using this metric, CausalODE outperforms the strongest competing method or baseline by approximately 60% on the CaRPool-seq knockdown dataset and 80% on the Norman et al. activation dataset. Its top-ranked edges generally show greater enrichment for high-confidence evidence from cell-type-matched ChIP-seq, CollecTRI, and regulatory STRING than those of other methods. The inferred graphs also distin-guish non-additive from approximately additive genetic interactions in held-out perturbation pairs. Finally, ablation analyses show that optimizing causal reach improves performance on held-out perturbations, and the learned latent regulator activities track simulated protein dynamics, with median temporal correlations ranging from 0.79 to 0.99.

title: Single-nucleus long-read RNA sequencing reveals isoform usage shifts in mouse acute kidney injury.
abstract: Single-cell and single-nucleus short-read RNA sequencing has elucidated transcriptomic changes across kidney cell types at the gene expression level. However, its limited read length precludes reliable isoform identification, hindering the characterization of individual protein-coding isoforms and non-protein-coding isoforms. We combined long-read sequencing with single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing technologies to investigate isoform regulation in healthy and acutely injured mouse kidneys. Single-cell and single-nucleus long-read RNA sequencing datasets were generated from kidneys of three healthy adult male C57BL/6J mice. An additional three adult male C57BL/6J mice underwent bilateral renal ischemia-reperfusion injury, and kidneys were subjected to single-nucleus long-read RNA sequencing. A total of 1.3 billion reads were generated, with a median read length of 757-884 bases across samples. Single-nucleus libraries yielded a smaller proportion of reads assigned to isoforms than single-cell libraries, reflecting their larger proportion of intronic reads. Nevertheless, single-nucleus libraries detected more distinct isoforms and greater isoform expression diversity, partly owing to the near absence of mitochondrial gene-derived transcripts. Single-nucleus analysis of healthy and injured kidneys revealed that ischemia-reperfusion injury downregulated oxidative phosphorylation- associated genes in proximal tubule cells both at the gene expression level and through shifts in isoform composition. Beyond oxidative phosphorylation-associated genes, Fut9 and Prrc2b were identified as genes exhibiting prominent shifts in isoform usage after ischemia-reperfusion injury. Single-nucleus long-read RNA sequencing detected injury-induced shifts in isoform usage in mouse kidney, adding a layer of transcriptomic information that is largely inaccessible to conventional gene-level short-read analysis.

title: GFAP upregulation by astrocytes attenuates tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology in a mouse model of tauopathy.
abstract: The upregulation of the intermediate filament glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) by reactive astrocytes has been traditionally assigned structural functions such as the shaping of astrocyte morphology and the formation of the glial scar. However, in vitro studies have also implicated GFAP in chaperone-mediated autophagy and endolysosomal trafficking. Here we hypothesized a role of GFAP in proteostasis in neurodegenerative proteinopathies. Specifically, we tested whether GFAP upregulation by reactive astrocytes helps control phospho-tau (pTau) neurofibrillary tangle burden in vivo. We investigated the interactome of GFAP in human control and AD brains via co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) followed by mass spectrometry. We also overexpressed GFAP in the astrocytes of THY-Tau22 mice using a viral transfer approach and characterized downstream effects on astrocyte phenotype, pTau burden, and neurodegenerative measures by combining immunohistochemistry, biochemistry, RNA-sequencing, and co-IP/mass spectrometry. We show that the interactome of GFAP immunoprecipitated from human control and AD brains is unexpectedly enriched in proteostasis effectors. Overexpressing GFAP in astrocytes of THY-Tau22 mice reduced hippocampal pTau neurofibrillary tangle burden, increased presynaptic marker levels, and modulated neuronal c-Fos expression, with more pronounced effects in female mice. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis revealed an induction of genes involved in extracellular matrix and small GTPases mediating cytoskeleton dynamics, whereas co-IP/mass spectrometry revealed an extensive network of proteostasis-related interactors, including components of endocytosis/macropinocytosis, lysosomal autophagy, heat shock protein response, and the ubiquitin-proteasome system. These findings challenge the conventional view of GFAP as a mere scaffold protein of the astrocyte cytoskeleton and suggest a novel role of GFAP in proteostasis with potential neuroprotective effects.

title: Nsun5 deficiency leads to impaired myelin integrity and sleep disruption.
abstract: Sleep disruption is common in disorders involving white-matter abnormalities, but the molecular pathways linking ribosomal RNA modification to disordered sleep remain unclear. NSUN5, which encodes an rRNA methyltransferase, is deleted in most patients with Williams-Beuren syndrome (WBS), a condition frequently accompanied by sleep problems. This clinical association suggests that loss of NSUN5 may contribute to sleep dysfunction, potentially through mechanisms relevant to white-matter integrity and neural activity. We combined electroencephalography/electromyography phenotyping, transcriptomics, ribosome profiling, nascent proteomics, proteomics, electron microscopy, positron emission tomography-computed tomography, and pharmacological rescue experiments in Nsun5-knockout mice to define how loss of Nsun5-dependent 28 S ribosomal RNA 5-methylcytosine affects white-matter integrity and sleep. Nsun5 deficiency markedly reduced 28 S rRNA m5C levels and led to selective translational dysregulation rather than global translational failure. The affected translational programs were enriched in myelination-related pathways and voltage-gated potassium channel subunits, including Kcna1 and Kcna2. At the cellular and tissue levels, these alterations were associated with oligodendrocyte loss, diffuse hypomyelination of the corpus callosum, and increased regional cortical metabolic activity. Correspondingly, Nsun5-knockout mice exhibited reduced non-rapid-eye-movement sleep and altered nocturnal sleep organization. Treatment with clemastine significantly improved sleep abnormalities and restored myelin integrity, while treatment with 4-aminopyridine also alleviated the sleep phenotype. These findings suggest that Nsun5-dependent rRNA methylation contributes to sleep disruption in association with white-matter dysfunction and altered potassium-channel-related protein abundance. Our results provide a preclinical framework for understanding sleep disturbances associated with WBS and other myelin-related neurological conditions.

title: Integrating k-mer GWAS and time-series transcriptomics to dissect the genetic architecture and immune defense networks against pokkah boeng disease in polyploid sugarcane.
abstract: Pokkah boeng disease (PBD), caused by Fusarium sacchari, is a devastating fungal disease that threatens global sugarcane production. Understanding the genetic basis of PBD resistance is crucial for molecular breeding under sugarcane's complex autopolyploidy. Here, we evaluated an F1 population of 201 individuals derived from a cross between 'ROC22' (resistant) and 'Zhongzhe 1' (susceptible). Based on multi-year field trials and artificial inoculations, we established a robust phenotypic evaluation system using Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (BLUP) values. A k-mer-based genome-wide association study (GWAS) identified 759 associated loci, highlighting 22 stable major-effect loci detected across multiple environments. Time-series RNA-seq analysis revealed the transcriptional dynamics of infection, pinpointing 48 h post-inoculation (hpi) as the critical time point for resistance-susceptibility divergence. By integrating physical mapping with temporal expression patterns, we identified four key candidate genes: the sensor DUF4220, the signaling switch Ras-family protein, the defense executioner DDE superfamily endonuclease, and the homeostasis regulator T-complex protein. This study outlines a four-dimensional (perception-transduction-execution-monitoring) immune framework, revealing the molecular mechanisms by which resistant genotypes construct multiple defense barriers through precise temporal coordination. The identified major-effect loci and core genes provide pivotal targets and a scientific foundation for marker-assisted and genomic selection in sugarcane disease-resistance breeding.

title: EP300 drives the progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma by regulating NUPR1-mediated ferroptosis and EMT.
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which E1A binding protein p300 (EP300) drives OSCC progression, focusing on its regulation of Nuclear Protein 1 (NUPR1)-mediated ferroptosis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). An OSCC xenograft mouse model was established using CAL-27 cells in BALB/c nude mice. In vitro experiments were performed using OSCC cell lines (CAL-27, SCC-25). Clinical relevance was assessed using 16 pairs of human OSCC and adjacent non-tumor tissues. Key techniques included RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry (IHC), Western blotting, qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, and a range of functional assays (CCK-8, EdU, TUNEL, Transwell) to evaluate cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and invasion. Ferroptosis was assessed via flow cytometry for reactive oxygen species (ROS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and MDA/GSH kits. EP300 was significantly upregulated in OSCC tissues. EP300 knockdown suppressed cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT. Mechanistically, EP300 was found to transcriptionally upregulate NUPR1. Silencing NUPR1 phenocopied these anti-tumor effects and induced ferroptosis. Crucially, the effects of NUPR1 knockdown were reversed by the ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1. In vivo, EP300 knockdown suppressed tumor growth; this effect was rescued by NUPR1 overexpression but subsequently nullified by the ferroptosis inducer Erastin. EP300 drives OSCC progression by upregulating NUPR1, which in turn suppresses ferroptosis to facilitate EMT and enhance malignant phenotypes, suggesting that targeting this axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to inhibit OSCC metastasis.

title: ZNF469 couples amino acid transport and precursor biosynthesis to collagen production in fibrosis.
abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) drive liver fibrosis through excessive collagen deposition, a metabolic process that imposes a high supply of specific amino acids, including proline and glycine. Despite these requirements, the transcriptional networks that coordinate this metabolic supply chain remain poorly defined. In this study, we identified the zinc-finger protein ZNF469 as an important transcriptional regulator of amino acid transport and precursor biosynthesis in HSCs. Using global RNA sequencing, we found that ZNF469 depletion in HSCs significantly downregulated multiple amino acid transporter (AAT) and collagen precursor enzyme genes, leading to reduced transporter and enzyme protein expression, impaired transport of collagen-relevant amino acids, decreased hydroxyproline synthesis, and diminished intracellular and extracellular collagen production. CUT&RUN profiling revealed that ZNF469 bound the regulatory regions of these genes, and promoter reporter assays confirmed that ZNF469 activates their transcription. In human liver tissues, AAT and collagen precursor enzyme genes were upregulated in fibrotic samples and positively correlated with ZNF469 expression. Reanalysis of transcriptomic data from ZNF469-depleted pulmonary and dermal fibroblasts suggest a conserved role for ZNF469 in regulating AAT and biosynthetic enzyme genes. Clinical dataset analysis from human fibrotic lung and skin tissues further revealed a positive correlation between ZNF469 and this metabolic gene signature. Functional rescue by amino acid supplementation and by restoration of a ZNF469-regulated transporter partially restored collagen production, and single-cell analyses localized this program to activated, disease-driving fibrogenic cells. Our findings support ZNF469 as an important transcription factor that helps coordinate amino acid influx with precursor biosynthesis to support collagen production. This regulatory network may represent a crucial mechanism contributing to fibrotic progression and a promising target for future therapeutic development in multi-organ fibrosis.

title: Transcriptomic insights into persistence and seasonal reactivation of corpora lutea in Iberian lynx (Lynx pardinus) and Eurasian lynx (Lynx lynx).
abstract: Monoestrous lynx species exhibit a reproductive adaptation unique among studied mammals: steroidogenically active corpora lutea (CL) persist beyond parturition and coexist with newly formed CL in subsequent reproductive cycles. Previous studies demonstrated seasonal changes in morphology, endocrine activity, and candidate-gene expression in lynx CL. However, the mechanisms underlying CL persistence and seasonal reactivation remain unknown. This study provides the first transcriptome-wide characterization of CL function in lynx species. RNA sequencing was performed on freshly formed CL (fCL) and in-season persistent CL (perCL-IS) collected from two Iberian lynx (Lynx pardinus), and out-of-season persistent CL (perCL-OS) collected from five Eurasian lynx (Lynx lynx). Differential expression, functional enrichment, and protein-protein interaction analyses identified pathways enriched in perCL-IS. Transcriptomic analyses revealed separation of fCL, perCL-IS, and perCL-OS, reflecting major transcriptional differences between CL groups. Comparison of fCL and perCL-IS identified 5039 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), while 2304 DEGs distinguished perCL-IS from perCL-OS. A total of 518 protein-coding genes were consistently overexpressed in perCL-IS relative to both other CL types. These genes were enriched in calcium signaling, ion transport, signal transduction, dynein complex, and metabolism. Comparative analyses identified overlap with genes associated with functional CL in domestic cat, dog, pig, and cattle. These findings demonstrate extensive seasonal transcriptomic remodeling of persistent lynx CL and identify calcium signaling, ion transport, and cellular maintenance pathways as candidate mechanisms supporting their functional persistence and seasonal reactivation. The generated data provides a foundation for development of assisted reproductive techniques to support lynx conservation breeding.

title: Spatial transcriptomics for gene discovery identifies Slc13a5 as a modulator of bone mechanoadaptation.
abstract: Bone is a dynamic tissue that continuously adapts its structure in response to mechanical loading, an essential process for maintaining skeletal health. However, this adaptive capacity declines with aging, contributing to increased fragility and fracture risk. Developing therapeutic strategies that preserve or restore bone mechanoadaptation in patients with increased bone fragility requires identifying key molecular regulators of this process. Because mechanoadaptive responses are spatially heterogeneous across bone compartments and loading environments, we applied spatial transcriptomics (GeoMx, NanoString) to characterize gene expression changes induced by mechanical loading in the female murine tibia, focusing on periosteal and bone compartments in regions under tension and compression. Spatial data were validated and cross-compared with previously published bulk RNA-seq and laser-capture microdissection datasets, identifying a set of 12 genes consistently regulated by loading across independent platforms and laboratories. Among these candidates, we selected Slc13a5 for in vivo investigation because it encodes a citrate transporter implicated in bone mineralization and metabolism, yet its role in bone mechanoadaptation remains unknown. Conditional deletion of Slc13a5 in osteolineage cells using Osteocalcin-Cre in female mice significantly increased the loading-induced mineralizing surface in tensile regions compared with Cre- Slc13a5fl/fl littermates. In addition, Slc13a5 cKO mice exhibited lower resorption around the neutral axis after loading compared to controls. Together, these findings identify Slc13a5 as a regulator of bone adaptation in regions experiencing low mechanical stimulation and suggest it as a potential therapeutic target for conditions characterized by impaired mechanoadaptive responses. This study highlights spatial transcriptomics as a powerful gene discovery framework for bone, enabling identification of novel targets to understand mechanisms and develop therapies.

title: SHMT2 K280 Succinylation Drives Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma Progression via S100A8+ Neutrophil-Mediated Immunosuppression.
abstract: Background: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) remains therapeutically challenging due to its aggressive biology and highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). While the contribution of protein succinylation to immune evasion is increasingly recognized, the specific succinylation events governing immunosuppression in ICC are poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate how succinylation drives TME remodeling to promote ICC progression and to identify potential therapeutic targets for improving patient outcomes. Methods: Succinyl-proteomic analysis of 10 pairs of ICC tumor tissues and adjacent normal tissues revealed that succinylation of serine hydroxymethyltransferase 2 (SHMT2) at lysine 280 (K280) was increased in ICC tumor tissues compared with paired adjacent normal tissues. Immunoprecipitation combined with mass spectrometry was used to identify lysine acetyltransferase 2A (KAT2A) as the enzyme mediating SHMT2 K280 succinylation. Subcutaneously implanted tumor models and hydrodynamic transfection-induced ICC models were used to investigate the in vivo role of SHMT2 K280 hyper-succinylation. Single-cell RNA sequencing, gene set enrichment analysis, and in vitro functional assays were conducted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms through which SHMT2 K280 succinylation remodels the TME. Results: We observed a significant elevation of SHMT2 K280 succinylation in clinical ICC specimens and identified this modification as a critical posttranslational modification that drove immunosuppression through a nonenzymatic signaling axis. Mechanistically, KAT2A-mediated SHMT2 K280 hyper-succinylation inhibited the proteolysis of FOS (Fos proto-oncogene, AP-1 transcription factor subunit), thereby enhancing FOS-mediated regulation of lipocalin-2 (LCN2) expression. Secreted LCN2 subsequently recruited and activated neutrophils expressing S100 calcium-binding protein A8 (S100A8) by binding to its receptor, solute carrier family 22 member 17 (SLC22A17). Neutrophil infiltration established an immunosuppressive microenvironment niche that potently impaired CD8+ T cell function and promoted tumor progression. Disruption of the SHMT2-LCN2 axis abrogated neutrophil-mediated immunosuppression and enhanced the efficacy of chemotherapy and immunotherapy in preclinical ICC models. Conclusions: We propose that combining LCN2 blockade with either gemcitabine/cisplatin or immune checkpoint inhibitors represents a precision strategy for ICC patients harboring SHMT2 K280 hyper-succinylation. Our work reveals a noncanonical, succinylation-driven mechanism by which SHMT2 modulates the immune landscape, and identifies LCN2 blockade as a therapeutically actionable target to increase the efficacy of both chemotherapy and immunotherapy in ICC.

title: Transcriptional profiles of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in major depressive disorder.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) has been associated with peripheral immune alterations, but transcriptional changes within the major T cell lineages remain poorly characterized. We performed bulk RNA sequencing of magnetically-enriched CD4+ and CD8+ T cell fractions from a cohort comprising 81 individuals with MDD and 48 healthy controls (HCs). Differential expression was assessed for protein-coding genes and long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), canonical T cell receptor (TCR)-segment transcripts were examined separately, and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis was used to characterize associated molecular pathways and upstream regulators. In CD4-enriched cells, 202 protein-coding genes and lncRNAs met a false discovery rate threshold of < 0.05, whereas no gene met this threshold in CD8-enriched cells. Twenty-one canonical TCR-segment transcripts, predominantly TRAJ genes, were increased in MDD. Pathway analysis implicated broad transcription- and chromatin-regulatory programs. Exploratory sex-stratified analyses identified a broader CD4+ signature in males, comprising 487 differentially expressed genes and including reduced cytotoxic/natural killer-like and major histocompatibility complex class I antigen-processing programs, together with increased TRAJ transcript abundance. These findings identify an MDD-associated peripheral transcriptional signature detected primarily in CD4-enriched cell fractions and characterized by distributed regulatory-state and TCR-segment changes. Together, this dataset provides a cell-type-resolved foundation for future studies examining the clinical relevance and functional consequences of CD4+ T cell transcriptional alterations in MDD.

title: Clinical validation of KIF11 overexpression in colorectal cancer and its potential association with the antitumor effects of nitidine chloride.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality with few effective targeted therapies. Kinesin family member 11 (KIF11), a motor protein essential for mitotic spindle assembly, is frequently overexpressed in multiple cancers. We hypothesized that nitidine chloride (NC), a natural benzophenanthridine alkaloid with documented anti-tumor activity, might suppress CRC by targeting KIF11.Molecular docking predicted a strong interaction between NC and KIF11 (- 9.0 kcal/mol). RNA sequencing, quantitative RT-PCR, and immunohistochemistry confirmed that NC treatment markedly downregulated KIF11 expression. Meta-analysis across public datasets showed consistent KIF11 mRNA overexpression in CRC (standardized mean difference [SMD] = 1.33; AUC = 0.87), while in-house immunohistochemistry on 416 clinical specimens demonstrated even stronger protein-level elevation (AUC = 0.99) that correlated with larger tumor size and deeper invasion. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics further revealed that KIF11 is preferentially expressed in proliferative malignant epithelial cells. Through CRISPR-based knockout screening and lentiviral silencing, KIF11 depletion impaired the growth or viability of the examined CRC cell models. Public ChIP-seq data suggested RAD21 occupancy near the KIF11 regulatory region, whereas reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation supported an association between the RAD21 and KIF11 proteins. Among genes co-expressed with KIF11,a pronounced enrichment was observed in pathways governing cell-cycle progression. Following KIF11 knockdown, transcriptomic profiling showed reduced expression across cell-cycle, DNA-replication, and chromatin-cohesion programs, alongside a reciprocal increase in amino-acid metabolism and stress-response genes. At the functional level, KIF11 depletion suppressed cell proliferation and induced G2/M-phase arrest. Taken together, these in vitro and limited xenograft data indicate that NC restrains CRC growth chiefly through the RAD21-KIF11 axis; KIF11 represents a promising preclinical target, though comprehensive systematic in vivo pharmacodynamic and translational animal validation remains absent in the current study and requires further independent investigation.

title: Phase IB trial of the BMI-1 inhibitor unesbulin plus neoadjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin in advanced ovarian cancer.
abstract: Preclinical studies with BMI-1 inhibitor Unesbulin (PTC596) demonstrated enhanced anti-cancer activity. This trial was designed to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), preliminary efficacy, and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of Unesbulin combined with Paclitaxel (P) and Carboplatin (C) in advanced OC. The trial utilized a 3 + 3 design to determine the safety, maxium tolerated dose (MTD), and RP2D of Unesbulin + paclitaxel and carbplatin (PC) for 3 cycles, followed by surgery and 3-7 cycles of Unesbulin + PC. Blood samples were collected to estimate PK parameters. RNA was extracted and analyzed from pre- and post-therapy tumor samples. Unesbulin tablets were escalated up to 300 mg po twice weekly with PC with no DLTs. The most commonly reported treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were those associated with PC and included nausea and fatigue (48%), neutropenia (44%), vomiting (36%), diarrhea (28%) and anemia (20%). Most common grade 3 or higher TEAE included neutropenia (40%) and neutropenic fever (12%). Among 18 patients with measurable disease, the objective response rate before surgery was 61%. Unesbulin was detectable post-dose through 96 h, reaching Tmax at 4 h. Cmax and AUC0-24 h increased with the dose. RNA expression analysis revealed increased mitochondrial dysfunction, Granzyme A signaling, sirtuin signaling, antigen processing, and a concomitant decrease in oxidative phosphorylation (OP), complex I biogenesis, and NET signaling. The study demonstrates that unesbulin + PC is feasible and safe. Exploratory data showed the critical role of BMI-1 in regulating cellular bioenergetics and modulating the immune response, supporting BMI-1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy. Dose escalation was halted based on the sponsor's declaration of 300 mg PO twice weekly as the optimal combination dose, and the expansion cohort was not enrolled due to the company's de-prioritization of the asset. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03206645, on 2017-07-02.

title: The PTBP1-RORA axis is a central mediator of the cytotoxic T-cell response to multimodal thermal therapy in hepatocellular carcinom.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer mortality, necessitating therapies that bridge local tumor control with systemic anti-tumor immunity. While multimodal thermal therapy (MTT) can induce immunogenic responses, the precise molecular programs governing antigen-driven cytotoxic CD8⁺ T-cell immunity following ablation remain undefined. This study aims to delineate the transcriptional mechanisms driven by MTT that govern CD8⁺ T-cell mediated anti-tumor immunity. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic profiling and proteomic analyses were performed on clinical samples obtained from HCC patients treated with MTT. Functional assays, including cytokine production, cytotoxicity analyses, and molecular interaction studies, were used to characterize CD8⁺ T-cell effector programs. Genetic manipulation and conditional knockout models were employed to interrogate the mechanistic role of key regulatory factors in vivo using murine HCC models. Statistical analyses were conducted using appropriate parametric or nonparametric tests as indicated, with significance determined based on standard criteria. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that MTT drives a distinct differentiation trajectory of CD8+ T cells toward a highly cytotoxic state, which was strongly associated with elevated expression of the nuclear receptor RORA. CD8 + T cells isolated from MTT-treated tumor-bearing mice exhibited a robust anti-tumor effector program characterized by increased production of IFN-γ, Perforin, Granzyme-B, and the chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10, resulting in enhanced tumor cell killing. Mechanistically, the RNA-binding protein PTBP1 was identified as a critical co-activator of RORA. MTT treatment upregulated PTBP1, which directly interacted with RORA, facilitated its nuclear import, and promoted its recruitment to the promoters of cytotoxic effector genes. In murine HCC models, elevated RORA expression in CD8+ T cells was associated with enhanced anti-tumor responses following MTT. Notably, conditional deletion of Rora in CD8+ T cells completely abrogated the therapeutic efficacy of MTT. This study identifies the PTBP1-RORA axis as a central transcriptional regulator of CD8+ T-cell mediated anti-tumor immunity induced by multimodal thermal therapy. Our findings provide mechanistic insight into how MTT initiates systemic anti-tumor immune remodeling and reshapes cytotoxic T-cell function highlight PTBP1-RORA signaling as a promising biomarker and therapeutic target for enhancing cancer immunotherapy in HCC.

title: Gene-level RNA-seq obscures extensive transcript-level remodeling during hypoxic adaptation.
abstract: Although RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) generates transcript-resolved measurements, these data are commonly summarized to the gene level by collapsing sequencing reads into a single expression value for each gene. Because most mammalian genes express multiple transcript isoforms through alternative splicing and alternative promoter usage, this framework can obscure major changes in transcript composition and consequently misrepresent transcriptional responses. To determine the extent to which isoform-level regulation remains undetected by conventional analyses, we examined hypoxic stress responses in human vascular endothelial cells using complementary approaches that quantify differential exon usage, transcript usage, and alternative splicing across multiple durations of hypoxia. These analyses uncovered thousands of hypoxia-responsive genes not identified by gene-level approaches and revealed that the earliest response to hypoxia occurred predominantly through changes in transcript usage rather than overall expression, whereas later stages showed progressive convergence between the two levels of regulation. Notably, most alternatively spliced genes remained undetected by standard differential expression analyses throughout the time course, indicating that transcript remodeling frequently occurs independently of changes in total gene expression. Incorporating transcript-level information also substantially expanded the number of hypoxia-associated biological pathways, revealing regulatory programs not captured by conventional gene-level analyses. These findings demonstrate that gene-level RNA-seq substantially underestimates the complexity and temporal structure of hypoxic adaptation and identify transcript remodeling as a major and previously underappreciated component of the endothelial hypoxic response.

title: Transcriptomic and co-expression network analysis reveals coordinated multi-pathway regulation of blueberry fruit ripening.
abstract: Blueberries are valued for their colour, flavour, and high polyphenol content, particularly anthocyanins. Understanding the transcriptional regulation underlying fruit development and ripening is essential for improving fruit quality and nutritional value. This study aimed to characterise gene expression changes across key developmental stages in highbush blueberry and identify the molecular pathways associated with ripening. A two-year transcriptomic analysis was conducted on 'Chandler' highbush blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum) at three developmental stages: green (S1), expansion (S2), and fully ripe (S3). Messenger RNA libraries were sequenced, generating approximately 25 million paired-end reads per sample. Differential expression analysis identified 11,470 genes that showed significant differential expression between the green (S1) and fully ripe (S3) stages in both years, indicating extensive transcriptional reprogramming during ripening, whereas earlier transitions involved fewer changes. Functional enrichment revealed that early development was associated with cell wall modification processes, including pectate lyase and cellulase activity, while ripening stages were enriched for phosphatase and hydrolase activities. Weighted co-expression network analysis identified modules related to flavonoid biosynthesis, cell wall remodelling, antioxidant processes, signalling, and sugar transport. Key genes, including CYP75A1 and UGT90A1 (flavonoid biosynthesis), NCED1 (abscisic acid biosynthesis), XTH28 and BGAL8 (cell wall enzymes), PER42 and CuAOγ1 (antioxidant enzymes), and TORL3 (microtubule-associated protein), presented strong stage-specific expression patterns and high network connectivity. These patterns were consistent across both growing seasons. This study provides a systems-level view of blueberry fruit development, highlighting coordinated transcriptional changes across multiple biological pathways during ripening. The identification of conserved gene expression patterns and key regulatory candidates offers valuable targets for improving fruit quality and health-promoting traits in blueberry.

title: Landscape dynamic network biomarker analysis pinpoints nitrogen-induced transition states in the transcriptome of Arabidopsis thaliana.
abstract: Nitrogen signaling coordinates nutrient uptake, metabolism, and growth; although temporal transcriptional responses to nitrate have been mapped in terms of transcript abundance, whether the transcriptomic network undergoes a transient, critical-transition-like reorganization after nitrate resupply has not been examined. We reanalyzed a public time-series RNA-seq dataset (GSE97500; 0-120 min; n = 3 per time point) using a Dynamic Network Biomarker (DNB) framework, implemented through the Module Criticality Index (MCI) and a shrinkage-stabilized index of critical transition (Ic.shrink), to investigate early network alterations in Arabidopsis thaliana. We identified candidate critical transition states (CTSs) at approximately 30 min in roots and 60 min in shoots, within the temporal resolution of the data. These states were characterized by elevated transcript variability and increased intra-module correlation, alongside reduced inter-module connectivity. Approximately 52% of genes within the CTS-associated module overlapped with differentially expressed genes (DEGs), indicating that the network-based analysis provides information partly complementary to changes in mean abundance. Candidate CTS-associated genes, including WRKY40, DOF5.8, NRT2.3, and NLP7, were identified within the integrated protein-protein interaction (PPI) subnetwork. Mod​ule genes exhibited enrichment in nitrate transport, response to nitrogen compounds, and transcription factor activity. Furthermore, annotated members and PPI hubs suggested roles in hormone signaling, development, redox regulation, and stress responses. These findings suggest that DNB-based analysis can complement conventional transcriptomics by identifying candidate transition-associated network states. It is important to note that the inferred states are computational, based on three replicates, and restricted to transcript-level data; therefore, they are hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation.

title: Synovial DNA methylation signatures predict TNF inhibitor response in rheumatoid arthritis: an integrative multiomic and machine-learning analysis.
abstract: This study aimed to assess how effectively baseline synovial DNA methylation and transcriptomic data capture inflammatory states relevant to tumour necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) response in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and to compare their predictive utility. Synovial biopsies from etanercept-treated patients with RA in the Stratification of Biologic Therapies for Rheumatoid Arthritis by Pathobiology (STRAP) randomised controlled trial (RCT) underwent baseline genome-wide DNA methylation profiling (n = 54) and RNA sequencing (n = 67), with paired 16-week samples analysed in a subset (methylation: n = 14; RNA sequencing: n = 20). Differential methylation and transcriptomics were assessed by histological pathotype and response. Hierarchical clustering identified molecular subgroups, longitudinal analyses examined post-treatment changes by response, and baseline data were used to train machine-learning models using a nested cross-validation framework. Baseline synovial DNA methylation captures regulatory states reflecting tumour necrosis factor α (TNF-α)-driven inflammation across pathotypes and in subsequent responders. Forty-four significant response-associated differentially methylated regions were identified. Promoter hypomethylation of genes relevant to TNF-α signalling (IL32, ARID5B, and PRKCZ) was found in responders. Hierarchical clustering of DNA methylation and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) independently identified responder-enriched subgroups. TNFi treatment induced coordinated promoter hypermethylation of key TNF-α and interleukin-6 pathway genes in responders, whereas RNA-seq longitudinal changes reflected inflammatory resolution. A DNA methylation-only machine-learning model showed the highest performance for predicting TNFi response (median area under the curve (AUC) 0.83) compared to transcriptomic and multiomic models, with prediction driven by a compact 25-probe panel including probes at RA-relevant loci. Synovial DNA methylation captures stable baseline regulatory states reflecting TNF-α-driven inflammation that predispose to TNFi response and shows superior predictive performance compared with transcriptomics, supporting its utility for TNFi stratification.

title: scCont: Interpretable Contrastive Learning for Functional Characterization of Cellular State Transitions.
abstract: Timecourse single-cell RNA (scRNA) datasets have become indispensable biological tools for studying and uncovering the underlying regulatory processes driving continuous cell-state transitions such as the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. However, these highly fluid, non-linear gene program dynamics remain difficult to disentangle. While deep neural network models can effectively map complex topologies, they are biological black boxes, lacking the gene-level interpretability required by experimental practitioners. Here, we introduce scCont, a fully unsupervised contrastive learning framework for extracting interpretable functional transition units from scRNA-seq data. Rather than relying on explicit temporal labels or clustering priors, scCont uses an unsupervised k-nearest neighbors approach to project local transcriptomic neighborhoods into a low-dimensional embedding. During post-training analysis, scCont employs Shapley network attribution to determine gene-latent relationships, mapping latent dimensions directly into functional gene programs. We quantitatively and qualitatively validate this representation by demonstrating that scCont captures biologically interpretable dynamics more effectively than baseline methods such as LDVAE. Evaluated across 13 diverse EMT timecourse datasets and four simulated datasets, scCont exposes interpretable functional dynamics and effectively maps context-dependent functional groups, helping to bridge the gap between deep learning representation and translational biological utility. scCont is an open source software available on GitHub ( https://github.com/nramani611/scCont ).

title: Myeloid subpopulations correlate with responsiveness to therapy in a prospective, longitudinal study on RA patients.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease associated with the destruction of cartilage and bone, increased risk of cardiovascular disease and a higher mortality rate. Despite the many therapies that exist for RA, there is little information to guide selection of the most effective treatment for an individual patient. Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies have created an opportunity to investigate the target tissue. While a number of studies have characterized the stromal and immune cell populations using single-cell technology on synovial biopsy samples, here we performed a longitudinal study, where we collected comprehensive clinical data over a one-year period on each patient in the process of changing their therapy. Samples from minimally invasive, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were collected from RA patients at baseline prior to start of a new therapy and 4-6-week follow-up under IRB-approved protocols with informed consent. Comprehensive clinical data from each appointment were recorded into a shared REDCap database. Failure to respond to therapy was based on clinical disease activity index (CDAI) for RA after 12-18 weeks post therapy. Biopsied samples were dissociated, enriched for CD45⁺ or CD45⁺CD11b⁺ cells, and processed on the 10X Genomics Chromium platform to generate libraries for single-cell RNA sequencing with cell-surface protein detection (CITE-seq). Spatial transcriptomics were performed on formalin-fixed paraffin embedded sections analyzed with 10X Xenium and NanoString CosMx. We performed CITE-seq analysis on ∼38,000 CD45+ synovial cells isolated from 17 patients who failed a conventional or biologic DMARD and planned to change therapy. We then subclustered on the myeloid population to reveal 12 myeloid subpopulations that consist of macrophages (n = 8), Osteoclast-like cells, DCs (n = 2) and proliferating cells. The proportion of cDCs was significantly higher in responders, while the proportion of macrophages was significantly lower in responders. The proportion of ISG15 + and THBS1 + macrophages were enriched in the non-responder patients. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that ISG15 + macrophages were preferentially localized to the synovial lining, while the THBS1 + macrophages are likely interacting with lymphoid cells within the sublining tissue. These data are among the first to prospectively profile macrophage populations as predictors of response to therapy. Future studies are required to verify whether myeloid subpopulation associations hold across specific therapies.

title: Longitudinal miRNA-mRNA Profiling Reveals Network Reorganization in Preeclampsia.
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity. Temporal dynamics of molecular dysregulation across pregnancy remain poorly understood. We performed longitudinal RNA sequencing of maternal whole blood to characterize miRNA-mRNA regulatory network evolution in PE. Whole-blood samples from early (M1: 10-18 weeks) and late pregnancy (M2: 32-38 weeks) were analyzed from 43 PE cases and 106 normotensive controls, including 109 paired samples (36 PE cases, 73 controls). Differential expression, temporal classification, pathway enrichment, and miRNA-mRNA network integration were performed. Placental expression support was assessed using internal RNA-seq and public databases. Key miRNA-mRNA interactions were experimentally validated in HTR-8/SVneo trophoblast cells. PE exhibited marked temporal reorganization of miRNA-mRNA networks, with strongly opposing temporal effect sizes across overlapping miRNA and mRNA features (Spearman ρ = -0.82, P < 0.0001). PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 signaling showed biphasic reversal (NES = +1.46, FDR = 0.028 at M1; NES = -1.64, FDR = 0.025 at M2), and heme-metabolism programs showed progressive suppression (2.1-fold NES intensification; FDR < 0.05 at both timepoints). Network analysis identified 29 high-confidence biphasic miRNA-mRNA pairs, including convergent targeting of ADGRA2 by three miRNAs and HSD17B1 by three miRNAs. miR-101-3p overexpression reduced DEPP1 mRNA (∼40%) and protein (∼26%) in trophoblast cells (P < 0.01), supporting a FOXO-DEPP1 axis. Blood-derived pairs showed pathway convergence with placental VGLL3-centered programs (PI3K/AKT, FOXO, TGF-β, trophoblast differentiation). PE is associated with predominantly stage-specific or biphasic miRNA-mRNA network reorganization, with PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 dynamic remodeling and progressive heme-metabolism suppression. These findings support gestational-age-specific biomarker development and identify regulatory axes, including miR-101-3p → DEPP1, for mechanistic investigation. This study is an ancillary analysis from the VDAART, which is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT00920621 : https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00920621?term=vdaart&rank=1 ).

title: [Inhibitory Effect of Hydroxychloroquine on Monocyte-Macrophage-Mediated Cytokine Storm and Its Molecular Mechanism].
abstract: To investigate the regulatory effect of hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) on monocyte-macrophage activation, and to clarify its inhibitory effect and potential molecular mechanism in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced cytokine storm model. THP-1 cells were induced to differentiate into macrophages using phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), followed by LPS stimulation to construct a cytokine storm model. Based on the model group, cells were co-cultured with HCQ as the experimental group. Cell proliferation activity was detected using the CCK-8 assay, cell apoptosis was evaluated via Annexin V/PI double-staining flow cytometry, and macrophage activation levels were determined by flow cytometry. The levels of related cytokines were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Furthermore, transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed to explore the gene expression profile regulated by HCQ during cytokine storm, and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and Western blot were employed to verify the key regulatory molecules and elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. HCQ inhibited the proliferation and induced the apoptosis of monocytes, and these effects were more pronounced in activated monocyte-macrophages. Its mechanism may involve the downregulation of the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, the upregulation of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax, and the induced cleavage and activation of caspase-3, thereby inducing programmed cell death. Additionally, HCQ effectively suppressed the activation process of cytokine storm in monocyte-macrophages, and significantly reduced the levels of inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and TNF-α. Meanwhile, HCQ downregulated the expression of CXCL8 and CXCR1 in the CXCL8-CXCR1/2 chemokine axis, as well as CXCL12 in the CXCL12-CXCR4/7 axis. Mechanistic investigations revealed that these effects might be related to the inhibition of aberrant activation of the NLRP3/IL-17A and TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathways by HCQ. HCQ can attenuate the biological impacts of cytokine storm by regulating chemokine signaling axes and suppressing the aberrant activation of the NLRP3/IL-17A and TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathways. This study provides a basis for the basic research and potential clinical intervention of cytokine storm.
extra: Zhongguo Shi Yan Xue Ye Xue Za Zhi

title: A high-throughput functional 3D droplet microfluidic platform for function-to-transcriptome profiling identifies candidate lncRNAs associated with engineered NK cell function.
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cell-based immunotherapies show considerable promise for cancer treatment; however, their efficacy against solid tumors remains limited by functional heterogeneity and the restrictive tumor microenvironment. Engineered NK cells, including mesothelin-directed chimeric antigen receptor cytokine-induced memory-like (MSLN-CAR CIML) NK cells, exhibit enhanced cytotoxic potential, yet the transcriptional programs underlying effective tumor killing remain poorly defined. Although protein-coding regulators of NK cell function have been extensively studied, the contribution of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to cytotoxic NK cell states remains largely unexplored, particularly in engineered NK cell therapies. To address this gap, we developed and applied a three-dimensional (3D) Matrigel-based droplet microfluidic screening platform that enables single-cell resolution analysis of NK-tumor interactions. Unlike conventional bulk transcriptomic approaches, this function-to-transcriptome workflow enables functional isolation of killer and non-killer NK cell populations prior to transcriptomic profiling enabling the direct comparison of transcriptional programs associated with cytotoxic function while minimizing confounding effects of bulk population analyses. Using this approach, we profiled donor-matched MSLN-CAR CIML NK cells and CIML NK controls from three independent donors. Comparative transcriptomic analysis revealed widespread differences in lncRNA expression between killer and non-killer NK cell populations, characterized predominantly by broad lncRNA downregulation that was consistently observed across donors and more pronounced in MSLN-CAR CIML NK cells than in CIML controls. Integrated lncRNA-mRNA analyses prioritized candidate lncRNA-gene pairs based on genomic proximity and coordinated co-expression patterns, identifying several lncRNAs associated with cytotoxic gene programs. These transcriptional signatures were further associated with enrichment of cytotoxic and inflammatory pathways characteristic of highly functional NK cell states. Together, these findings demonstrate the utility of our functional droplet microfluidic screening platform in prioritizing candidate lncRNAs associated with cytotoxic NK cell states within matrix-restricted tumor environments. By integrating functional phenotyping with transcriptomic profiling, this platform provides a framework for identifying candidate lncRNA and other potential biomarkers associated with cytotoxic NK states for future mechanistic validation and the rational optimization of NK cell-based immunotherapies for solid tumors.

title: Hypoxia combined with vitamin C and N-acetylcysteine attenuates telomere shortening and replicative senescence in human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells.
abstract: Human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSCs) are promising candidates for regenerative medicine; however, prolonged in vitro expansion promotes oxidative stress, replicative senescence, functional deterioration, and telomere attrition. This study evaluated whether integrating physiological hypoxia with vitamin C (VC) and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) could maintain the quality of multiple dimensions of hUC-MSCs during long-term expansion. hUC-MSCs derived from three independent umbilical cord donors were cultured from passage 3 (P3) to passage 10 (P10) under normoxic (21% O₂) or hypoxic (5% O₂) conditions with VC and/or NAC supplementation. Cell proliferation, senescence, intracellular ROS-associated fluorescence, glutathione redox status, and multilineage differentiation potential were assessed using CCK-8, SA-β-gal staining, H2DCFDA-based flow cytometry, GSH/GSSG measurements, and lineage-specific differentiation assays, respectively. Relative telomere length and telomere signal-free chromatid ends were evaluated by Q-FISH, and telomerase activity was measured using the TRAP assay. RNA-seq and functional enrichment analyses were complemented by RT‒qPCR, Western blotting, and siRNA-mediated RTEL1 knockdown. The hypoxia + VC + NAC condition produced the most consistent overall protective profile during prolonged expansion. Treated hUC-MSCs for 10 passages maintained their proliferative capacity; exhibited reduced SA-β-gal positivity and intracellular ROS-associated fluorescence; showed an increased GSH/GSSG ratio; and retained adipogenic, chondrogenic, and osteogenic differentiation potential. Q-FISH demonstrated attenuation of the passage-associated decline in relative telomere fluorescence and a reduced frequency of signal-free chromatid ends. These changes were not accompanied by a detectable increase in telomerase activity. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enrichment of HIF-1, AMPK, glutathione metabolism, DNA repair, and telomere maintenance-associated programs, together with reduced inflammatory and senescence-related signalling. Independent RT‒qPCR confirmed increased RTEL1, CTC1, and WRN expression, and Western blotting validated increased RTEL1 protein expression. RTEL1 depletion increased p21 expression and SA-β-gal activity, partially reversing the anti-senescence phenotype induced by the combined culture conditions. Hypoxic culture combined with VC and NAC provides an effective, non-genetic strategy for reducing oxidative stress, delaying replicative senescence, retaining multilineage differentiation potential, and attenuating passage-associated telomere shortening during prolonged hUC-MSC expansion. RTEL1 contributes, at least in part, to the anti-senescent phenotype induced by the combined culture conditions.

title: AI-driven multi-omics identifies SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a therapeutic target and predicts lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that SPP1⁺ TAMs engage TM4SF1⁺ malignant epithelial cells via the SPP1-CD44 axis within a hypoxic niche, driving tumor stemness, invasion, and metastatic progression. SPP1⁺ TAMs exhibit a hypoxic, M2-polarized phenotype and their abundance correlates with worse overall and progression‑free survival in metastatic PTC patients. We further develop an integrative machine-learning model based on SPP1⁺ TAM‑derived molecular features that predicts lymph node status with high accuracy. Preclinically, pharmacological targeting of SPP1 attenuates tumor cell migration, invasion, and lung metastasis, supporting its candidacy as a therapeutic target. Collectively, this study demonstrates how AI‑driven multi‑omics analysis can jointly identify a functionally validated target and generate a clinically deployable predictive model, illustrating a framework for bridging computational discovery with translational oncology.

title: EPIGEN-Prostate: Identifying multi-omic markers of prostate cancer in Aotearoa New Zealand men.
abstract: DNA methylation biomarkers have demonstrated promise as potential clinical biomarkers for improved detection and risk stratification of prostate cancer (PCa). Despite this, only sparse genome-scale, sequencing-based DNA methylation data are available in the early PCa setting. The EPIGEN-Prostate study aims to identify novel cell-free DNA methylation biomarkers from blood and multi-omic biomarkers from prostate tissue for detecting clinically significant PCa (csPCa). EPIGEN-Prostate is a multi-centre, prospective, longitudinal cohort study of patients undergoing investigation for potential PCa, with a biomarker discovery-focused design. The primary objective of this study is to characterise novel cell-free DNA-based molecular biomarkers for non-invasive PCa detection and risk stratification. Secondary objectives include the development of multi-omic risk classifiers to predict disease progression and treatment response. The primary endpoint is the presence or absence of csPCa, defined here as International Society of Urological Pathology grade group ≥2. Secondary endpoints will include disease stage at presentation, disease recurrence following curative treatment, metastasis-free survival, and overall survival. Individuals aged ≥18 years, scheduled to undergo prostate biopsy, and able to provide informed consent are eligible to participate. Blood samples will be prospectively collected before prostate biopsy, and prostate biopsy tissue will be retrieved for analysis after regular processing. Participants proceeding to radical prostatectomy may contribute surgical tissue and serial postoperative blood samples. Pre-biopsy plasma and matched prostate tissue samples will undergo genome-wide DNA methylation profiling using reduced representation bisulfite sequencing approaches. Tissue samples will also undergo RNA sequencing and genetic profiling. Clinical outcomes will be collected for up to 15 years. Biomarker discovery and validation will integrate molecular and clinical data using nested case-control analyses for each objective. Not applicable. Human ethical approval was obtained via the New Zealand Health and Disability Ethics Committee - Southern (HDEC 21/STH/184).

title: Multi-source analysis identifies an NPC2-associated macrophage transcriptional program in ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves extensive remodeling of intestinal macrophage states, but the molecular programs linking inflammation, lysosomal function, and lipid handling remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify macrophage-associated molecules and cellular states linked to UC. We integrated UC single-cell RNA sequencing, bone marrow-derived macrophage polarization transcriptomes, UK Biobank OLINK proteomic associations, external bulk transcriptomic datasets, and spatial transcriptomics. Candidate molecules were further examined in dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis and macrophage activation models. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, receiver operating characteristic, and Spearman correlation analyses were performed as appropriate. Twelve genes were shared among UC-associated macrophage differentially expressed genes, macrophage polarization-related genes, and UC-associated circulating protein signals. NPC2 was prioritized based on its macrophage enrichment, external transcriptomic performance, and established lysosomal function. Single-cell reclustering identified an NPC2+MMP12+ macrophage subset with heterogeneous abundance across donors. Donor-level analysis showed a numerically higher median proportion of NPC2+MMP12+ macrophages in UC than in controls, but the difference was not statistically significant (17.7% vs. 9.3%; two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, P = 0.471). NPC2-high macrophages exhibited enrichment of lysosomal, phagocytic, complement, lipid-handling, antigen-presentation, and tissue-remodeling programs. Spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed a positive association between NPC2 expression and macrophage-related signatures in inflamed mucosal regions. NPC2 expression was also increased in DSS-induced colitis and inflammatory macrophage models. Cholesteryl sulfate sodium (CSS) reduced nitrite production and shifted macrophage marker expression away from CD86 predominance, although NPC2 dependence was not established. NPC2 is associated with a lysosome-related macrophage transcriptional program observed in UC. These exploratory findings support further investigation of macrophage lysosomal lipid handling and warrant functional and independent clinical validation.

title: Integrative ferroptosis-related bioinformatics identifies PPARγ as a therapeutic target of ursolic acid against inflammation and pathological osteogenesis in ankylosing spondylitis.
abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by persistent inflammation and aberrant new bone formation. Ferroptosis has increasingly been implicated in immune dysregulation and pathological bone remodeling; however, its molecular involvement in AS and its potential value for natural product discovery remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular targets in AS, screen natural compounds targeting the key candidate, and validate their therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms. Bulk RNA-seq datasets were combined to perform differential expression profiling, ferroptosis evaluation, weighted co-expression network construction, functional pathway annotation, and machine-learning-driven feature screening. Subsequently, single-cell transcriptomic data were examined to map the cell-type-specific localization of the hub genes that had been pinpointed. Natural product and compound-target databases were subsequently searched for small-molecule compounds associated with both AS and the key target. Candidate compounds were subjected to batch molecular docking. Based on its predicted binding properties and biological relevance, Ursolic acid (UA) was selected as a candidate drug. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the stability of the UA-PPARγ complex. The therapeutic effects of UA were subsequently examined in an AS mouse model and in BMP-2/4-induced osteogenic differentiation of fibroblasts. Histological staining, qRT-PCR, and western blotting were used to assess inflammatory responses, pathological osteogenesis, and PPARγ-related signaling. Integrated transcriptomic analysis identified 20 genes shared among AS-related differentially expressed genes, ferroptosis-related genes, and genes from ferroptosis-associated co-expression modules. Machine-learning analysis further identified PHF21A, PPARG, and TP53INP1 as hub genes, among which PPARG showed the highest predictive contribution and distinct expression patterns across immune cell populations. Database-based natural product screening and batch molecular docking identified UA as a promising PPARγ-targeting candidate. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported a potential interaction between UA and PPARγ. In vivo, UA markedly alleviated inflammatory infiltration, reduced the expression of TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-17, and attenuated pathological bone formation in AS mice. In vitro, UA increased PPARγ expression while suppressing the osteogenic markers COL1A1, ALP, RUNX2, OPN, and BMP-2, thereby inhibiting the osteogenic transdifferentiation of fibroblasts. This study established an integrated strategy combining ferroptosis-related bioinformatics analysis, machine-learning-based target identification, natural product screening, molecular simulation, and experimental validation. PPARγ was identified as a ferroptosis-associated molecular target in AS, and UA exerted concurrent anti-inflammatory and anti-osteogenic effects accompanied by increased PPARγ protein expression. These findings suggest that targeting PPARγ with UA might be a potential therapeutic strategy for AS.

title: Galectin-1 identifies a unique subpopulation of highly invasive glioblastoma cells and enables their migration.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM), the most common primary brain tumor, is characterized by extensive infiltration into surrounding brain tissue. GBM tumors exhibit substantial intratumoral heterogeneity making it difficult to identify and target invasive cell subpopulations. Here, we use an in vitro model of the mechanical transitions at the tumor-brain interface to isolate highly invasive GBM cells from populations derived from unique patient tumors. Using single-cell RNA sequencing combined with cell barcodes we were able to trace distinct cell lineages during migration and identify an invasive subpopulation which preferentially migrates across stiffness interfaces. This mechanically sensitive invasive subpopulation exhibits a transcriptomic profile characterized by overexpression of galectin-1, a β-galactoside binding protein. Our findings reveal that galectin-1 expression level positively correlates with invasion rate and inhibition of galectin-1 binding to cell surface glycoproteins prevents migration. This study identifies galectin-1 expression is a characteristic of invading GBM cells in mechanically defined interface model where galectin-1 may serve as an important maker to identify and target invasive GBM cells.

title: Transcriptome-based machine learning classification of pediatric germ cell tumors using nanopore RNA sequencing.
abstract: Childhood cancer comprises a heterogeneous group of diseases, with disproportionately higher mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) due to limited access to molecular diagnostics. Pediatric germ cell tumors (GCTs) are rare and represent 3% of childhood cancers, showing substantial clinical and biological heterogeneity, which makes accurate subtype classification challenging. As part of an ongoing multicentric collaboration, we evaluated nanopore whole-transcriptome sequencing as a scalable approach for differentiating pediatric GCTs from other solid tumors and distinguishing their histological subtypes using a nanopore-based transcriptomic classifier. Nanopore RNA-seq was performed on 56 pediatric tumors, including 14 germinomas/dysgerminomas/seminomas, 13 yolk sac tumors, 11 mature teratomas, seven immature teratomas, eight mixed tumors, and three embryonal carcinomas. A machine learning model was trained using their gene expression profiles and followed by independent validation. Transcriptome data enabled molecular classification, achieving 98.9% overall accuracy in distinguishing GCTs from other previously sequenced pediatric solid tumors, and 100% accuracy above the established confidence threshold of 0.8. GCT subtype classification achieved 90.3% overall accuracy and 89.8% above 0.8 prediction probability. The model showed high F1-scores and AUC values above 0.86. Consistent performance was maintained in an independent cohort, and transcriptomic profiles derived from FFPE samples showed high concordance with cryopreserved tissues, supporting the method's applicability in routine clinical specimens. These results demonstrate the diagnostic potential of the developed pipeline for GCT subtyping and support its future application in decentralized or resource-constrained healthcare systems. By enabling transcriptome-based classification with minimal infrastructure, nanopore platforms offer a promising solution for improving cancer diagnostics in LMICs.

title: NKAIN1 predicts poor prognosis and associated with drug resistance and immune infiltration in prostate adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Na, K-ATPase interaction 1 (NKAIN1) is a transmembrane protein that can interact with Na, K-ATPase β1 subunit. NKAIN1 has prognostic value in several cancers, but its biomarker and carcinogenic roles in the development of prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD) remain underexplored. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database were used to analyze the expression and prognostic significance of NKAIN1 in PRAD. The Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC) database and The Cancer Therapeutics Response Portal (CTRP) database were used to analyze drug resistance. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to define cell clusters. GO, KEGG, and GSEA enrichment analyses were performed to predict the function of NKAIN1-related factors. Finally, CCK8, Colony formation assay, transwell experiments, and subcutaneous tumor formation in nude mice were conducted to validate the role of NKAIN1 in PRAD development. NKAIN1 was significantly upregulated in PRAD, correlating with advanced TNM stages, poor survival, and may be involved in drug resistance. High NKAIN1 expression was associated with altered immune infiltration. Additionally, NKAIN-related genes were enriched in Wnt signaling, metabolism, and immune-related pathways. Knockdown of NKAIN1 suppressed PRAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and immune evasion in vitro and tumor growth in vivo. NKAIN1 serves as a prognostic, drug resistance, and immune infiltration marker. Moreover, NKAIN1 promotes PRAD progression and suggests it acts as a potential therapeutic target. This research has been retrospectively registered in the Ethics Committee institutional of the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University with the number of 2025-733.

title: ROS-responsive Se@HSC-DIA enables local drug delivery and modulates CD44high inflammatory nucleus pulposus cell states in intervertebral disc degeneration.
abstract: Low back pain is closely associated with structural abnormalities of the spine, yet how altered mechanical loading drives persistent disc inflammation and pain remains unclear. Here, we investigated the cellular mechanisms linking structural disturbance to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) and developed a mechanism-guided local therapy. Human disc specimens from patients with lumbar spondylolysis (LS), integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets, primary nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs), pharmacological perturbation, and an in vivo IVDD model were analyzed. LS-associated discs showed increased NOX4 and CD44 expression with enhanced oxidative stress and inflammation. Single-cell analysis identified a CD44high inflammatory NP population (Inflamed NP) that expanded with degeneration severity. Oxidative stress promoted this state, whereas IL-1β-IL-1R1 signaling and canonical NF-κB activation sustained its inflammatory and matrix-catabolic phenotype. Drug screening identified diacerein (DIA) as an effective inhibitor of this axis. We therefore developed Se@HSC-DIA, an injectable hydrogel that responds to reactive oxygen species (ROS) and integrates CD44 affinity, ROS-triggered DIA release, and selenium nanoparticle-mediated antioxidant activity. Se@HSC-DIA reduced ROS, NF-κB activation, inflammatory mediators, and matrix catabolism in NPCs. In vivo, it preserved disc structure, restored matrix homeostasis, alleviated pain-related behavior, and shifted the degenerative transcriptome toward homeostasis without evident systemic toxicity. These findings define a ROS-IL-1β/IL-1R1-NF-κB axis linking structural stress to an inflammatory NP state and support microenvironment-responsive biomaterials for IVDD therapy.

title: DNA methylation signatures from tissue and cell-free DNA in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency mirror clinical pathologies providing a potential non-invasive tool to monitor liver disease progression.
abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a serpinopathy in which mutations in the SERPINA1 gene cause misfolding of alpha-1 antitrypsin (Z-AAT), leading to hepatic protein accumulation, proteotoxic stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite a uniform genetic mutation in most affected individuals, liver disease severity varies, reflecting contributions from environmental exposures and epigenetic heterogeneity (e.g. DNA methylation). As RNA-interference therapy has emerged as a promising treatment, understanding how epigenetic variation relates to the clinical and histopathologic features of AATD may provide insight into disease heterogeneity, progression, and therapeutic response. We analyzed a longitudinal cohort of ZZ-genotype AATD patients with paired liver biopsies, plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and clinical data collected at baseline and 3-y follow-up. Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of liver tissue identified 15 CpG clusters associated with liver disease severity, immune pathways, and clinical measures including METAVIR fibrosis score and γ-glutamyltransferase. Parallel methylation profiling of matched plasma-derived cfDNA identified eight analogous CpG clusters enriched for similar biological pathways and associated with clinical parameters. Integration of tissue and cfDNA datasets revealed fifty-one shared CpGs representing disease-associated methylation signatures, including loci such as ZFP57 that tracks with portal inflammation. We also identified a DNA methylation signature associated with fibrosis progression based on changes in METAVIR score. These findings demonstrate that liver- and cfDNA-derived DNA methylation signatures robustly stratify AATD patients by relevant measures of liver injury and fibrosis, supporting their potential as non-invasive biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring responses to emerging therapies.

title: Targeting autocrine CCL2 signaling reveals oncogenic networks and prognostic biomarkers in medulloblastoma.
abstract: CCL2 is a well-established mediator of immune cell recruitment to the tumor microenvironment (TME), however, its autocrine role in medulloblastoma remains poorly understood. This study investigated the molecular and prognostic consequences of CCL2 ablation in medulloblastoma cells. CCL2 expression was characterized in HTB-186 medulloblastoma cells, and CRISPR/Cas9 was used to generate CCL2 knockout (KO) cells. Transcriptomic alterations were assessed by RNA sequencing followed by differential gene expression, KEGG pathway, and Gene Ontology analyses. Select signaling pathways were validated by cytokine and protein analyses. The prognostic significance of differentially expressed genes was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses in the Cavalli medulloblastoma cohort (n = 488). HTB-186 cells expressed high levels of CCL2, and approximately 40% of cells expressed the CCL2 receptor CCR2, supporting the existence of autocrine signaling. CCL2 ablation resulted in 2, 284 differentially expressed genes and significantly altered pathways involved in PI3K/Akt, NF-κB, JAK/STAT, cAMP, and Hippo signaling. These transcriptomic findings were confirmed by reduced IL-6 production and altered activation of Akt, NF-κB, CREB, and YAP. Survival analyses identified four genes upregulated following CCL2 knockout (KSR2, DLG4, DGKA, and PLD2) that were associated with improved overall survival, whereas four downregulated genes (HSPA8, MYC, CCND1, and ETS2) were associated with poorer survival. These associations remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, metastatic status, histology, and molecular subgroup. Our findings demonstrate that autocrine CCL2 signaling regulates multiple oncogenic pathways in medulloblastoma and promotes transcriptional programs associated with tumor growth, survival, and poor clinical outcome. These results identify CCL2 as a potential therapeutic target and highlight CCL2-regulated gene signatures as candidate prognostic biomarkers in medulloblastoma.

title: MCT4-Associated Lactate Export Defines Myeloid Metabolic Reprogramming during Head and Neck Cancer Progression.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) development is accompanied by metabolic remodeling of the tumor microenvironment, yet how metabolic programs evolve across specific cell populations during tumor progression remains poorly understood. We integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from five HNSCC cohorts comprising 645,351 cells from 114 patients and inferred metabolic flux using single-cell Flux Estimation Analysis (scFEA). Myeloid cells showed the highest and most consistent metabolic allocation to lactate export among major cell types. In ten patients with paired normal mucosa and carcinoma, myeloid lactate-export allocation increased from 1.72% to 3.31% of total inferred metabolic flux, with an increase in every patient. SPP1+ macrophages showed the highest lactate-export allocation in carcinoma. Lactate export was predominantly associated with MCT4/ SLC16A3 . In carcinoma, myeloid SLC16A3 expression exceeded SLC16A1 by 17-fold, and CPTAC-HNSCC confirmed tumor enrichment of MCT4 protein. Together, these findings identify increased MCT4-associated lactate export as a prominent feature of myeloid metabolic reprogramming during HNSCC progression.

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis dissects hepatocyte states and genetic regulation of hepatic metabolism in pigs.
abstract: Hepatic metabolism is influenced by both the multi-tissue environment and cellular heterogeneity, yet the cellular basis and genetic regulatory mechanisms underlying liver-specific metabolic functions remain incompletely understood. Pigs share high similarity with humans in liver structure, physiological function, and metabolic characteristics, making them an important large-animal model for studying hepatic metabolic regulation. In this study, we integrated bulk RNA-seq data from 300 liver, spleen, and blood samples with liver scRNA-seq data to characterize pig hepatic metabolic regulation across tissue, cellular, and genetic layers. Multi-tissue transcriptomic analysis identified liver-enriched gene sets mainly associated with metabolic and synthetic functions, highlighting the functional specialization of the pig liver in a multi-tissue context. At single-cell resolution, hepatocytes were further resolved into two major subtypes. Functional annotation, trajectory analysis, and cell-cell communication analysis further showed that these two hepatocyte subtypes displayed distinct functional features: Hepatocytes_Metabolic was enriched for lipid metabolism and core hepatic pathways, whereas Hepatocytes_Immune was more closely associated with immune-related microenvironmental regulation. To investigate the genetic basis of cellular heterogeneity in liver tissue, we incorporated estimated cell-type proportions into cell-type interaction eQTL models.
