This analysis identified 6,313 ct-ieGenes across liver cell populations, with Hepatocytes_Metabolic showing the largest number of ieGenes (3,404), indicating that the proportion of this metabolic hepatocyte subtype provides an important cellular context for resolving heterogeneity in hepatic genetic regulation. Colocalization analysis further linked ct-ieQTL signals in Hepatocytes_Metabolic to liver-related biochemical and lipid traits, including gamma-glutamyl transferase and cholesterol-related traits. Cross-species analysis showed that pig hepatocytes were transcriptionally closer to human hepatocytes than to mouse hepatocytes, and pig-human conserved hepatocyte genes were mainly enriched in lipid metabolism-related functions. Overall, this study provides a multi-level framework for understanding pig hepatic metabolic regulation and suggests that Hepatocytes_Metabolic represents an important cellular context linking liver metabolic function, cell-composition-associated genetic regulation, and liver-related complex traits.

title: A single-cell transcriptomics-based prognostic model identifies TM4SF1 as a key promoter of malignant progression in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Intratumor heterogeneity in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) profoundly influences tumor progression and immune evasion. However, current prognostic models largely fail to capture the complex cellular dynamics of the tumor microenvironment (TME) at single-cell resolution. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing with bulk transcriptomics to derive cell-type-specific signatures. A systematic evaluation of 101 machine learning algorithm combinations was performed across multiple independent cohorts to construct a robust prognostic model. Immune landscape, mutational features, intercellular communication, and immunotherapy responsiveness were comprehensively evaluated. The biological functions of the identified hub gene, transmembrane 4 L six family member 1 (TM4SF1), were rigorously validated in vitro. The optimal StepCox[forward]-Ridge model showed strong prognostic stratification in five cohorts. Low-risk tumors exhibited an immune-inflamed phenotype, suggesting greater predicted good responses to immune checkpoint blockade. In contrast, high-risk tumors had an immunosuppressive TME with overactive cell communication driven by fibroblasts and myeloid cells. TM4SF1 was a key driver in this high-risk signature. TM4SF1 silencing significantly inhibited LUAD cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and strongly induced apoptosis. TM4SF1 depletion reversed tumor immune evasion by reducing PD-L1, increasing MHC-I, and lowering the secretion of CCL5. This single-cell-guided machine-learning framework provides strong prognostic stratification in LUAD and captures immune phenotypes associated with potential immunotherapy responsiveness. TM4SF1 emerged as a candidate mediator associated with malignant progression and immune-related phenotypes in LUAD, warranting further mechanistic and in vivo investigation. This suggests it could be a useful therapeutic target.

title: The Increase of Tuft Cells is the Pathological Feature of Nasal Mucosa Type 2 Inflammation, and Indicates the Poor Prognosis of CRSwNP.
abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is a common chronic airway disease, and eosinophilic CRSwNP (eCRSwNP) is associated with poor prognosis. Tuft cells are associated with type 2 inflammation, but their role in CRSwNP remains unclear. Public single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from nasal mucosal tissues of 21 participants (5 healthy controls, 5 patients with CRSsNP, 5 patients with non-eosinophilic CRSwNP, and 6 patients with eosinophilic CRSwNP) were evaluated, and bulk RNA sequencing, immunofluorescence, and protein correlation analyses were employed to investigate the association between tuft cells and the nasal mucosal type 2 inflammatory microenvironment. A total of 111 participants undergoing nasal surgery were recruited, and 69 CRSwNP patients with over 1-year follow-up were included in the prognostic analysis. CellChat and CellPhoneDB were utilized to explore the communication patterns between tuft cells and type 2 inflammation-related immune cells. Three-fold cross-validated LASSO-Cox regression was used to screen predictors for constructing a prognostic model. Tuft cells were increased in eCRSwNP and closely associated with type 2 inflammation severity. Moreover, tuft cells were predicted to interact with type 2 inflammation-related immune cells through arachidonic acid metabolites, acetylcholine, and galectin-9. Tuft cell signature genes were closely related to prognosis of patients with CRSwNP. A prognostic model combined with TRPM5 and tissue eosinophil (EOS) counts exhibited high predictive efficacy (AUC = 0.956 in training set, 0.904 in validation set). Tuft cells are increased in eCRSwNP and are associated with the severity of nasal mucosal type 2 inflammation. The tuft cell signature genes, especially TRPM5 combined with tissue EOS counts, can effectively predict the disease control status of CRSwNP patients after functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS). TRPM5 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for eCRSwNP, providing a perspective for precise diagnosis and treatment.

title: Single-cell transcriptome-based identification of core keratinocyte biomarkers and targeted drug discovery for atopic dermatitis.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory skin disorder driven by epidermal barrier impairment and keratinocyte dysfunction. Current therapies are limited by insufficient target specificity and high recurrence rates. This study aimed to identify keratinocyte-derived biomarkers and develop novel targeted agents for precise diagnosis and treatment of AD. Single-cell RNA sequencing and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed to screen for key AD biomarkers, and machine learning algorithms with ROC curve analysis were applied to evaluate their diagnostic performance. Immunohistochemistry confirmed LYPD3 protein upregulation in AD lesional skin. In silico knockdown simulations at single-cell resolution elucidated LYPD3-mediated signaling pathways. Structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations identified candidate LYPD3-targeted compounds, and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and biolayer interferometry (BLI) validated target engagement and direct binding. An in vitro keratinocyte inflammation model and an in vivo MC903 (calcipotriol)-induced AD mouse model were established to assess therapeutic efficacy. LYPD3, KRT6C, and FABP5 were specifically overexpressed in AD keratinocytes, showed excellent diagnostic performance that was validated in a fully independent external cohort, and correlated closely with cutaneous immune infiltration. LYPD3 depletion disrupted epidermal barrier integrity and keratinocyte differentiation pathways. CETSA confirmed target engagement, and BLI demonstrated direct binding between Rebastinib and LYPD3. Rebastinib inhibited keratinocyte hyperproliferation and inflammation in vitro and significantly ameliorated epidermal lesions while suppressing Th2-type inflammatory responses in AD mice. These findings identify three keratinocyte-specific AD biomarkers and support Rebastinib as a promising LYPD3-targeted therapeutic candidate, offering new insights into precision diagnosis and targeted therapy of AD.

title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses characterize an IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern in extracellular matrix remodeling and Treg-associated immune suppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is characterized by extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. As an important N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its downstream regulatory network and potential role in immune microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood. Public datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed to identify prognostic IGF2BP3-related genes. Functional enrichment analysis, prognostic model construction, immune infiltration analysis, somatic mutation profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomic analysis, and CellChat-based cell-cell communication analysis were performed. In vitro experiments, including qRT-PCR, western blotting, wound healing, transwell, CCK-8, and RNA stability assays, were conducted to evaluate the cellular effects of IGF2BP3 silencing. Multiplex immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, an orthotopic syngeneic mouse model, drug sensitivity analysis, and molecular docking were further performed to explore immune microenvironment associations and potential therapeutic implications. IGF2BP3 was significantly upregulated in PAAD and associated with poor prognosis. MMP1, MMP7, and ITGA2 were identified as candidate IGF2BP3-associated ECM-related genes. IGF2BP3 knockdown was associated with changes in the proliferation, migration, and invasion of Panc-1 cells and was accompanied by decreased stability of these transcripts. A prognostic signature consisting of IGF2BP3, MMP1, MMP7, and ITGA2 demonstrated consistent prognostic stratification across multiple independent cohorts. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed predominant expression of these genes in epithelial cell populations and highlighted their potential association with PAAD-related cellular states and intercellular communication. Among the downstream targets, MMP7 emerged as a candidate downstream effector based on RNA stability assays, SHAP feature importance analysis, gene interaction network analysis, and single-cell expression profiling. Both IGF2BP3 and MMP7 were positively associated with regulatory T-cell (Treg) infiltration. Spatial transcriptomic analyses further demonstrated significant spatial correlations among IGF2BP3, MMP7, and Treg-enriched immune niches, while multiplex immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, and an orthotopic syngeneic mouse model supported their association with immunosuppressive microenvironment features. Drug sensitivity analysis computationally prioritized Trametinib as a candidate for further investigation in high-risk PAAD, while molecular docking suggested favorable predicted interactions between Trametinib and the four signature proteins. IGF2BP3 was associated with PAAD progression, and its depletion was accompanied by reduced stability of ECM-associated transcripts and changes in the tumor immune microenvironment. Integrated bulk transcriptomic, single-cell transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, and experimental analyses identify MMP7 as a candidate downstream effector associated with IGF2BP3 and suggest that the IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern is related to Treg-enriched immunosuppressive niches in PAAD. Furthermore, Trametinib was identified as a hypothesis-generating therapeutic candidate for further evaluation in high-risk PAAD.

title: Proximity-aware Transcriptomics reveals non-random genomic clustering of low-annotated ncRNAs near protein-coding genes in SMA iPSCs.
abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic studies frequently dismiss cryptic, low-annotated non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) represented solely by Ensembl gene identifiers as functional noise due to a lack of curated nomenclature. To overcome this limitation and systematically decode this uncharacterized transcriptome, we developed the Proximity-aware ENSG Pipeline (PEP). PEP is a multi-layered computational framework that integrates differential expression processing, Ensembl-based biotype classification, linear genomic proximity modeling, and chromosome-conditional permutation testing. We deployed PEP on total RNA-seq data generated from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from patients with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) and healthy controls and validated key predictions with RT-qPCR. PEP captured the primary causal genetic lesion of SMA validating the biological baseline. Our framework demonstrated that low-annotated ncRNAs form a highly organized, gene-centered class-level architecture, remaining non-randomly proximal to protein-coding genes with an observed median neighbor distance of 14.6 kb versus a random null expectation of 74.2 kb. Under SMA ground-state conditions, the dysregulated subset of these ncRNAs exhibited tight, same-direction transcriptional cis-coupling with their nearest protein-coding partners, a phenomenon independent of genomic imprinting caveats. This transcriptional coupling was primarily directional, with an additional modest magnitude correlation, consistent with shared local transcriptional co-regulation. RT-qPCR corroborated RNA-seq directionality in all tested ncRNA-neighbour pairs, three-of-four reaching statistical significance, and confirmed three disease-ground targets. These findings reframe non-coding transcriptomic disruptions in SMA from isolated events into a genomically organized, locally coupled transcriptional phenomenon. PEP provides a scalable, reproducible workflow for the functional interpretation of low-annotated ENSG loci across diverse disease models.

title: A machine learning-assisted hypoxia-associated prognostic model reveals PFKP-mediated glycolytic regulation in uveal melanoma.
abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is a highly aggressive intraocular malignancy with strong metastatic propensity and poor response to immunotherapy. Hypoxia profoundly reshapes the tumor microenvironment and drives immune evasion. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-assisted hypoxia-related prognostic model and identify relevant metabolic candidates associated with UM progression. RNA-sequencing and clinical data from 80 UM patients were obtained from TCGA. Thirty highly connected hypoxia-related genes were prioritized through protein-protein interaction analysis and evaluated using five complementary survival-based machine learning approaches: LASSO-Cox, CoxBoost, random survival forest, XGBoost-Cox, and Survival-SVM. Genes supported by at least three of the five methods were defined as core candidates and further evaluated by multivariable Cox regression to construct the prognostic model. The prognostic relevance of the model was evaluated in the dependent GSE22138 cohort using metastasis-free survival (MFS) as the clinical endpoint. Survival analysis, ROC, PCA, GSEA, and immune microenvironment analyses were performed. PFKP was further examined for its associations with immune features and experimentally validated through in vitro and in vivo assays. Multi-algorithm consensus identified PFKP, ENO3, and FOXO3 as core candidate genes. PFKP showed the strongest cross-model consistency and was supported by all five methods, whereas ENO3 and FOXO3 were supported by four methods. Multivariable Cox regression retained ENO3 and PFKP as the final prognostic genes, yielding a parsimonious two-gene risk model that was further evaluated in the independent GSE22138 cohort. Higher risk scores were associated with worse overall survival in TCGA-UM, shorter MFS in GSE22138, and more advanced disease. Hypoxia- and glycolysis-related pathways were enriched in the high-risk group, which also exhibited higher immune and stromal scores, lower tumor purity, and increased expression of immune checkpoint genes. PFKP expression was positively associated with CD8+ T-cell infiltration and immune checkpoint-related gene expression. Functionally, PFKP knockdown reduced UM cell proliferation, migration, and glycolytic activity in vitro and suppressed xenograft tumor growth in vivo. We established a cross-algorithm hypoxia-related prognostic framework for UM. ENO3 and PFKP constituted the final prognostic signature, while PFKP, supported by all five algorithms and experimental validation, emerged as a functionally relevant glycolysis-related candidate associated with UM progression.

title: Single-cell analysis reveals smoke-induced neutrophil-macrophage crosstalk as a targetable mechanism in COPD pathogenesis.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is projected to become the third leading cause of death globally by 2030, with cigarette smoke (CS) exposure accounting for 80-90% of cases. This study aimed to elucidate the intercellular communication networks amplified by CS exposure and identify targetable pathways driving smoking-related COPD pathogenesis. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis of lung tissues from nine COPD patients stratified by smoking status (GSE173896), integrating ligand-receptor interaction inference (CellChat), pseudo-temporal trajectory analysis (Monocle), phenotype-cell linkage (Scissor), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) with bulk RNA-seq data (GSE57148). Smoking-associated immune cell subpopulations were identified, and pathogenic gene modules were prioritized through functional enrichment analysis. Key computational predictions were validated in C57BL/6 mice exposed to cigarette smoke for 90 days, with assessment of pulmonary function, histopathology, serum cytokines (ELISA), immunofluorescence, Western blot, and lung myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity. After quality control, 40,500 cells were analyzed (28,630 from COPD and 11,870 from never-smoker control tissues). At the sample level, COPD tissues showed a lower proportion of NK cells than controls (FDR = 0.011) and a trend toward more macrophages. Intercellular communication analysis revealed neutrophils and macrophages as dominant signaling hubs, and ANXA1-FPR1/FPR2 was among the most prominent neutrophil-to-macrophage ligand-receptor pairs. Trajectory analysis followed by sub-clustering and Scissor analysis prioritized macrophage and neutrophil subpopulations associated with the COPD phenotype in bulk lung tissue. Enrichment analysis of these modules pointed to neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and HIF-1 signaling. In vivo validation confirmed CS-induced pulmonary dysfunction, elevated serum cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6; all p < 0.05), increased macrophage infiltration with FPR2 upregulation (p < 0.01), neutrophil accumulation (p < 0.01) and NET formation, increased lung MPO activity (p < 0.001), and HIF-1α protein induction (p < 0.001). CS exposure drives chronic pulmonary inflammation through a self-amplifying neutrophil-macrophage circuit mediated by HIF-1α-induced NET formation and dysregulated ANXA1-FPR2 signaling. This study establishes intercellular crosstalk networks as central mechanisms linking environmental tobacco exposure to COPD pathogenesis. Single-cell profiling stratified by environmental exposure may inform early biomarker development and guide pathway-specific interventions for smoke-related lung diseases.

title: Identification of metabolism-associated biomarkers with a focus on ketone body pathways in diabetic retinopathy by integrating transcriptomics and single-cell analysis.
abstract: To identify potential biomarkers of ketone body metabolism (KBM) associated with diabetic retinopathy (DR), and to explore possible underlying mechanism between KBM and DR. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between DR and healthy normal control (NC) samples were acquired in GSE221521.Then, DEGs and KBM-related genes (KBM-RGs) were interleaved to discern candidate genes, and the key feature genes were derived through two algorithms of machine learning. Next, biomarkers were generated through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves analysis and expression validation in GSE221521 and GSE189005.Then, enrichment analysis, immune infiltration and single-cell RNA sequencing analysis were conducted.Finally, experimental validation of biomarkers was conducted through reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). ACACA and WDTC1 were recognized as DR-associated candidate biomarkers. ACACA was enriched in Reactome RNA polymerase II transcription pathway, and WDTC1 was enriched in Reactome eukaryotic translation initiation pathway. Two types of immune cells, namely activated NK cells and monocytes, were significantly different between DR and NC samples in bulk immune infiltration analysis. Next, NK cells and T cells were identified as key cell types based on cell proportion analysis. Both ACACA and WDTC1 were highly expressed in NK cells and T cells. Cell-cell communication patterns changed in the DR group. ACACA and WDTC1 showed stable expression during the differentiation of T cells and NK cells. Finally, RT-qPCR results showed that ACACA and WDTC1 were up-regulated in DR samples. This concurred with the results yielded by bioinformatics analysis. This study identified two metabolism-associated biomarkers (ACACA and WDTC1) that may serve as DR-associated candidate biomarkers. These preliminary findings suggest potential molecular leads for further investigation, though prospective validation in larger cohorts is needed.

title: MSX2 is an ERα-associated transcription factor that sustains proliferative capacity and is associated with favorable prognosis in luminal breast cancer.
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy among women and exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity. Luminal tumors represent the largest molecular subtype and are primarily driven by estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), a hormone-dependent transcription factor (TF) that regulates gene expression programs controlling proliferation, differentiation, and endocrine response. Herein, the study aimed to identify functionally relevant TFs regulated by ERα as part of a complex regulatory program in luminal BC. An integrative transcriptomic approach was applied to identify TFs regulated by ERα in luminal BC. Differential gene expression analysis was integrated with RNA-seq data obtained from estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1) gene knockdown conditions. Network and enrichment analyses were conducted to reveal ERα-centered transcriptional programs. Key TFs acting as potential ERα-regulated mediators were evaluated for subtype-specific expression in BC patient cohorts and for associations with patient survival. MCF7 and T47D cells underwent a time course of hormone deprivation, and the gene expression patterns of two TF candidates were assessed. Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats-associated protein 9 (CRISPR-Cas9)-mediated gene knockout experiments were performed to interrogate the functional roles of the ERα-regulated candidate TFs. The integrative transcriptomic analysis identified 95 ERα-associated candidate genes. Network and enrichment analyses highlighted ERα-centered regulatory pathways with nine genes encoding TFs. Among these TFs, Msh homeobox 2 (MSX2) displayed a subtype-associated expression pattern in BC patients and was associated with favorable survival outcomes. Hormone deprivation significantly altered the expression of MSX2 in BC cell lines, which pinpoints the functional regulation by ERα. Time-course evaluation of MSX2 under hormone-deprived conditions confirmed that MSX2 may be regulated by ERα. Furthermore, functional interrogation using CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene disruption demonstrated that the loss of MSX2 significantly impaired the proliferative capacity and viability of luminal BC cells. These functional assessments identified MSX2 as an underexplored ERα-associated TF and suggest that the ERα-MSX2 regulatory relationship may contribute to transcriptional programs associated with luminal BC identity and cellular fitness.

title: An EFHD1-associated ADSC niche modulates treatment response in experimental models of ER-positive breast cancer.
abstract: Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) modulate the breast cancer (BC) microenvironment, but their role in endocrine therapy resistance and clinical outcomes remains ill-defined. By integrating single-cell and multi-cohort bulk RNA-seq data from ER⁺ BC patients, we built an ADSC-derived prognostic model via a four-dimensional filtering strategy and 10 machine-learning algorithms. Spatial transcriptomics, co-culture assays, and orthotopic mammary fat-pad model validated the hub gene's function and mechanism. ADSCs were enriched in non-responders and exhibited elevated stemness. A 17-gene Ridge regression model stratified patient risk across five cohorts, with high-risk tumors showing TP53 mutations and immunosuppression. EFHD1 emerged as the key hub gene spatially co-localized with ADSCs. Mechanistically, co-culture with ER⁺ BC cells upregulated EFHD1 in ADSCs by ∼2.0-fold, which triggered NF-κB/p65 nuclear translocation and a ∼1.5-fold increase in FN1 protein levels. Functionally, EFHD1-overexpressing ADSCs promoted BC proliferation and invasion. In an orthotopic xenograft model, tumors co-injected with control ADSCs reached ∼500 mm³ by day 30 and maintained robust growth under letrozole + ribociclib (∼350 mm³), compared with BC cells alone (∼300 mm³). In contrast, EFHD1 knockdown in ADSCs reduced tumor volume to ∼200 mm³ and further sensitized tumors to letrozole + ribociclib (∼150 mm³, a ∼40% reduction relative to the drug-only group), with Ki-67 positivity decreasing from ∼4.0% to ∼1.5%. We established a robust ADSC-based prognostic model and uncovered a novel stromal EFHD1/NF-κB/FN1 axis driving ER⁺ BC progression and endocrine therapy resistance, identifying stromal EFHD1 as a candidate target whose pharmacological validation remains to be established.
